Working With the Guided Mode What Is the Guided Mode?

pdf_name: Amadeus Selling Platform Connect 23.2 User Guide - Apr2020 (2).pdf
paragraph: The Guided Mode lets you enter key information about the travel services offered, helping you create a relevant form or decide whether a form is needed or not. How to Create a Form in Guided Mode 1. Change the Country of the point of sale if needed. The law according to which the form is produced and the type of form are dependant on this selection. Note: The traveller's nationality and the travel destination are not relevant when selecting the country. 2. Select the form Language. Depending on the selected country, you may be able to choose from several available languages.

pdf_name: Amadeus Selling Platform Connect 23.2 User Guide - Apr2020 (2).pdf
paragraph: 3. Start typing the name of the provider and select the provider from the list. If the provider is not in the list, enter the full name and click on New. If you are entering the provider of a package holiday, you must also add the insolvency insurance. See How to Add Insolvency Insurance for a Provider on the previous page. Select the option Travel Agency Acts as Tour Operator if you are bundling travel services and selling them as a package under one invoice. 4. If the service offered is a package, check the Package Holiday check box. 5. If the service offered is not a package, enter the price and select the type of service and the time of booking. 6. To add more than four travel services, click on Add Further Travel Service. 7. Click on Create Form. The Amadeus Form Wizard uses the data you have entered to determine what type of form is needed. 8. Chapter 17: Timatic Getting Started With Timatic What Is Timatic? Timatic is a graphical application that replaces the Amadeus Timatic cryptic entries. It allows you to check travel requirements directly in the IATA database using your IATA credentials. To search for and check travel information, you can either: Manually add the passenger and itinerary details.

paragraph: Chapter 18: Document Management Understanding Document Management What Is Document Management? Document Management is an online storage system for documents created in Selling Platform Connect. All document types, such as receipts, invoices and quote documents are automatically stored as PDFs. From the Document Management module, you can retrieve, print or download any document that was created by your office: See Searching for Documents in Document Management below. See Printing and Downloading a Document on the next page. What Are Sensitive Documents? Legal documents or documents that cannot be easily recreated are considered sensitive and should be saved locally and kept by travel agents. The following are considered sensitive documents: Credit notes. E-ticket receipts. EMD documents. EMD receipts. Invoices. Payment receipts. Refund and exchange authorizations. Refund notices. Ticket documents. All German documents. Searching for Documents in Document Management How to Search for Documents 1. In the Main Page menu, click on Document Management. Use the date fields to retrieve documents that were created in a specific date range. The maximum date range that you can define depends on the selected document type. c. Use any of the other search fields to find the required documents.

Chapter 19: Profile Manager Getting Started With Profile Manager What Is Profile Manager? Profile Manager enables the automated management of bulk profile data in the Amadeus Customer Server (CSX) database. You can: Export all traveller and company profile data from selected offices. Count all active traveller and company profiles in selected offices. Import profiles using specific profile data in a customised input file. Delete profiles based on their record locators. ETG is currently sending out a high amount of emails to our customers where we are asking them to get back to us with their bank details to be able to process their refunds. The reason for the increased amount of emails is due to the long wait time to get the funds from the airlines, combined with our workload, which has resulted in many expired transactions in the PSP's. It is no longer possible to process the refund through them and therefore, we need to go ahead with a Bank transfer instead. We could expect a high amount of customers calling due to these emails. They might be concerned or worried if these emails are actually sent from us. It is therefore important for all agents to know that we are sending these, and the emails are legit. There should be a note in Edvin from BO stating that this email has been sent from E-track. The template used is the following: (standard template in Etrack) Dear Sir/Madam, We are contacting you because we need more information to process your refund. More specifically, we require your bank details. Please provide us with your IBAN, BIC/SWIFT, the name of th bank and the card holder's name and home address. Please write the IBAN number with dots or spaces after every third digit so it doesn't become encrypted. You consent to the handling by following this link <@CONTACTFORMLINK> Best regards, <@USERFULLNAME> <@BRANDNAME>

12. FareLogix: How to display an old EMD record What is EMD? An Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) is an electronic non-flight document that may be issued and used for the collection and settlement of optional services offered by an airline. There are two types of EMDs: Stand-alone EMD (EMD-S) Used independent of an e-ticket for services such as ground transportation, deposits and residual value. Associated EMD (EMD-A) Linked to an electronic ticket (ET) at the coupon level. Multiple EMDAs can exist for a single ticket. An EMDA coupon is considered used once its associated flight coupon is used. Baggage or seat upgrades are more likely to be issued on an EMDA, but whether a service is issued on an EMDA or EMDS depends on the individual airline. In which scenario we might need to issue EMD?

These services are also referred to as ancillary services and include such options as preferred seating, baggage, and deposits. Systems we issue EMD and responsibility to re-associate them.

13. SC Script notification visible in Edvin SC Workmode Step 1 - Starting point SC Script Automation What is the SC script ? Etraveli group has an automation for schedule change notifications in GDS systems. This automation is called Touchless in Amadeus, PBA in Sabre and ICM in Galileo, and it handles the ‘minor’ schedule changes automatically. How does it work? Wherever a schedule change occurs, the airline always places the PNRs in a GDS queue (Q5 or Q6) under each office ID. The script gathers those notifications in one office ID and then, according to the settings we have set, either automatically handles the minor schedule changes or places them in another queue for manual handling.

pdf_name: Content - 04. Schedule change GDS Automation (SC Script) 20250310-070237.pdf
paragraph: In order to automatically handle a SC case, we have set up the configurations (1) and added an airline table with policies (2). What configurations do we have? (1) The settings we currently use for automatically handling minor SC in all the GDSs are:

pdf_name: Content - 04. Schedule change GDS Automation (SC Script) 20250310-070237.pdf
paragraph:
1. Airline should provide us with a valid alternative (UN,TK or TK) 
2. There should be no misconnection between the flights (MCT) 
3. The schedule change that occurred should be within 23.5 hours 
4. The schedule change that occurred should not have a date change. Note: each GDS system has its own unique way of automatic handling. The settings we currently use for manual handling in all the GDSs are: 1. Airline has not provided a valid alternative (UN flights) 
2. There is a misconnection between the flights (MCT) 
3. The schedule change is more than 23.5 hours 
4. There is a date change (Original trip: 6 August 22:00/- New time: 7 August 00:30) 
5. There are VI and VI Bcom orders included What is an airline table with policies? (2) Each airline provides us with the policy we should follow for schedule changes. For example endorsement, OSI line, how we should reissue the ticket, etc. The airline table contains all this information for each system in one place, and should be manually updated every time we have a new policy from the airlines. Note, that some of the airlines might request from us to contact them for authorization for each case. Those airlines are excluded from the airline table. This means that the script will always place such PNRs into the manual handling queue. What if the script cannot handle a case automatically? The script handles a case according to the settings we have set up but if the process fails on any automated step (e.g.

pdf_name: Content - 04. Schedule change GDS Automation (SC Script) 20250310-070237.pdf
paragraph: the reissue or revalidation fails, or an error occurs), then the script will place the order on the Ticketing Q, and the Ticketing team will pick up the ticket and reissue it. Note: According to our settings, it is possible to exclude an airline if, according to the policy of the carrier, we need to get an authorization before any action. In such cases, the script will never process the schedule change notification for those airlines and will always place it on manual queue for processing in accordance with the RM lines and our settings (for example VI orders or NZ airline - authorization required). What do the OSI/remark lines mean?

Legislation is the process of making or enacting laws, as well as the set of laws or legal rules that have been formally established by a governing body, such as a parliament or congress. This process typically involves drafting, debating, and voting on proposed laws, called "bills," which, if approved, become enforceable rules within a particular jurisdiction. Legislation is essential for organizing society, establishing rights and responsibilities, regulating conduct, and providing a legal framework for resolving disputes. It can cover various areas like criminal law, civil rights, economic policy, health care, and environmental protection. Legislation ETG should follow 1. US DOT Rule 14 US DOT Rule 14 What is US DOT Rule 14 Overview of US DOT Rule 14.

Summary US DOT Rule 14 (The United States Department of Transportation) ensures passengers have a clear right to refunds, timely information on significant schedule changes, and protection in cases of overbooking. Airlines and ticket agents are required to follow specific guidelines to protect passenger rights, ensuring passengers are informed and compensated when necessary. Purpose Protects passenger rights when airlines oversell flights or make significant schedule changes, including automatic refunds and compensation for denied boarding. Applicability Covers U.S. and foreign airlines for flights to, from, or within the United States. US DOT Rule 14 1. Key Provisions of DOT Rule 14 Step 3 2. How it is going to affect our handling? Step-by-Step Guidelines: Handling of the SC Script Automation for US DOT in Amadeus and Step 6 Sabre Key Provisions of DOT Rule 14 1. Automatic Refunds Refunds are required when: The flight is cancelled by the airline. The airline makes a significant change to the flight schedule. Refund Timeline: Refunds must be processed within 7 business days for transactions through credit/debit cards and 20 days for cash or check purchases. The seven business day deadline starts running when the agent receives confirmation of the passenger's refund eligibility from the airline.

Additional Info: Airlines (including for codeshare and interline) are obligated to provide refunds if flights are cancelled Business days are considered to be from Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays in the United States.

2. Definitions of affected flight CanceledFlight A flight that was published in a carrier’s Computer Reservation System (CRS) at the time of the ticket sale, and not operated by the carrier. SignificantChange Defined changes to the itinerary which include: Departure Change: Leaving 3+ hours earlier (domestic) or 6+ hours earlier (international) than originally scheduled. Arrival Delay: Arriving 3+ hours later (domestic) or 6+ hours later (international) than originally scheduled. Rerouting: Departure or arrival at an airport other than originally scheduled. Additional Stops (Stopover): Increased number of stops compared to the original itinerary. Downgrade in Service: Moved to a lower class of service. Impact on Passengers with Disabilities: Involving different connecting airports or changes to accessibility features on aircraft. 3. Entities Responsible for Refunds Airlines and Ticket Agents who act as merchants of record (entities listed on customer billing statements) are responsible for issuing refunds. Ticket Agents (as defined in 49 U.S.C. 40102(a)(45)): Includes any person or business that sells or arranges air transportation as a principal or on behalf of airlines. 4. Informing Customers of Refund Eligibility Notice Requirement: Airlines and ticket agents must inform customers of their right to a refund before offering any travel credit, vouchers, or alternative travel arrangements.

Sample notification to customers about their refund options before alternative arrangements are offered in the 1st Alternative template. ATTENTION, once you identify that the rule is applicable to use the correct template. Additional information (Redirect to airline) NOTE: Additional information is not relevant to our travel agency, in such cases please redirect tomer to the airline. 5. Overselling and Denied Boarding (Involuntary and Voluntary) Overbooking: Airlines may sell more seats than are available to account for no-shows. Volunteer Process: Airlines must first seek volunteers to give up seats in exchange for compensation.

Involuntary Denied Boarding: If not enough passengers volunteer, airlines may deny boarding involuntarily but are required to provide compensation and protections for these passengers. 6. Compensation for Involuntary Denied Boarding Compensation Levels: Based on the time delay and alternative travel arrangements provided to passengers. Rights Notice: Passengers denied boarding involuntarily should be provided a written notice explaining their rights and the compensation they are entitled to. Exceptions of the rule: Compensation may not be required if a passenger fails to meet check-in requirements or if there are security or safety concerns. Airlines aren’t obligated to compensate for delays due to factors beyond their control, such as extreme weather or air traffic control issues. (FM) Rule 14 also requires that airlines fully disclose their policies regarding denied boarding, including how volunteers are compensated and how the airline decides who will be denied boarding involuntarily. This rule aims to make sure passengers are treated fairly and informed of their rights in cases of overbooking. Manual handling task under SC WM Step 1: Verify Airport Locations - Check the Flight Itinerary: Review the flight details to identify if any of the following airports are located within the United States: - Origin Airport (where the journey starts) - Arrival Airport (final destination) - Stopover Airport(s) (any intermediate stops) Example: If a flight has a stopover in New York, this itinerary includes a U.S. airport, which would trigger U.S DOT rules for consideration. Step 2: Confirm the Schedule Change (SC) Duration

For International Flights: Verify if the schedule change results in a delay or timing change of 5 hours or more from the original schedule. For Domestic Flights: Verify if the schedule change results in a delay or timing change of 3 hours or more from the original schedule. Action: Label the Case: Select the type of schedule change and label the case as U.S. DOT. Automated Evaluation: Systems like FLX (LHG), Tripstack, Amadeus NDCx, and Travelfusion will automatically check if there is a U.S. segment in the order. If so, the agent will receive a notification to confirm the labeling as "U.S. DOT" by selecting Yes or No. The logic developed as below: "Trivial" or "No Schedule Change": Will mark as non-US DOT "Minor" or "Force Majeure": Will not mark anything and will leave it for agents to select "Major" or "Critical": Will mark it as US DOT.

What Happens When the Customer Selects a Refund After Labeling the Case as U.S. DOT? If the customer opts for a refund in response to the case being tagged as U.S. DOT, the case will already be labeled appropriately in the "Manual Handling Queue" flow. The U.S. DOT tag ensures that the case is automatically prioritized in the refund dashboard, facilitating faste processing in accordance with U.S. DOT Rule 14. Chat, Phone, Email tasks Step 1: Verify Airport Locations Check the Flight Itinerary: Review the flight details to identify if any of the following airports fall within the United States: C Origin Airport (where the journey starts) O Arrival Airport (final destination) O Stopover Airport(s) (any intermediate stops) Example:IfaflighthasastopoverinNewYork thisitineraryincludesaU.S.airport.

Step 2: Confirm the Schedule Change (SC) Duration For International Flights: Check if the schedule change results in a delay or timing change of 6 hours or more from the original schedule. For Domestic Flights: Check if the schedule change results in a delay or timing change of 3 hours or more from the original schedule. Example:A7-hourdelayonaninternationa flightdepartingfromLosAngelesm etsthecriteria.

Step 3: Apply U.S. DOT Rule If the above criteria are met (U.S. airport involved + timing threshold), the U.S. DOT Rule applies. Action: Phase 0 - Check the airline policy and act accordingly while informing the customer on your actions. If applicable, use the relevant US DOT template (with refund option first one). Add clear errand notes of your investigation. Step 5 How it is going to affect our handling? Phase 1 Overview As part of the recent updates to meet regulatory and operational requirements, the following adjustments are being implemented in how we handle schedule changes: 1. Revised Templates: Schedule change notifications only for US market templates, which are being updated to align with new requirements, ensuring clarity and compliance. 2. Refund Alternatives: Refund options will now be presented as the first alternative in 1as Alternative templates to comply with customer rights requirements. 3. Language Adjustment: The language used for refund options will be adapted to a more neutral, generic tone for consistency across communications. 4. Automated Handling (0-5 Hours): Schedule changes affecting flights by 0-5 hours will be processed automatically using the normal routine of the Schedule Change Script flow in GDS. Further details on the script functionality are available here. 5. Manual Handling for Longer Schedule Changes / Changes Over 5 Hours: Any schedule change exceeding 5 hours will require manual handling by agents. 1.

Agents will process these changes either within the Workmode (WM) or outside it, depending on the tool’s capabilities (Outside WM: VI and multi-order scenarios). 2. Note for Manual Processing: Agents should move the refund option to the top of the list when handling cases outside the WM. 6. Priority Payout Processing: Approved refunds will be prioritized and processed within 7 days following airline approval, meeting new compliance requirements for timely refunds ONLY for US DOT Ruleaffected orders. Step 6 Step-by-Step Guidelines for Identifying and Handling the SC Script Automation for US DOT in Amadeus and Sabre

A new automation has been implemented in both Amadeus and Sabre based on the system-script configuration. This automation is designed to evaluate two specific conditions: Segments within the US Flight changes greater than 5 hours Once these conditions are met, the automation will automatically perform a set of actions. Here’s what agents need to do to identify and manage this process: Step 1: Automated SC Script Template Sent. The automation will trigger the sending of a specific SC script template for US DOT. This template will include: Refund Option with a link labeled “Contact Us” for any customer inquiries. Step 2: Label the Case as "US DOT" in SC WM. After the SC script template is sent, label the case as "US DOT" in the SC WM. This labeling ensures that the case is properly categorized and tracked according to the US Department of Transportation guidelines. Step 3: Close the Case. Once the case is labeled, proceed to close the case. This step marks the case as completed in the system:

Step 4 Which cases do we consider FM? Force Majeure (FM) occurs when an extraordinary event or circumstance beyond the control of the parties, such as the pandemic of COVID-19, massive strikes, weather conditions, bankruptcy, or political situations, prevents an airline from operating flights. In such cases, airline companies usually provide exceptional policies and guidelines that we have to follow, and these might change constantly. Thus, we should check our Edvin documents regularly to see any new updates that might have been published. These cases are handled by all FL agents. The status of the flight may be confirmed (HK) and/or affected by involuntary cancellation/schedule change (UN/TK). If there is an FM policy for handling a specific ticket, you may handle it further and offer passengers all possible alternatives. Whenever you see UN, UN/TK, TK, or TK/HX, we should consider these as SCs, and the SC team will handle them as well.

Since there is no possibility of separating FM and SC cases by looking at the status of the tickets, we have decided that the SC team will check the COVID-19 and FM TA policy as well, and if there is no restriction from the airline side, then agents will handle it as an SC case. When an FM situation occurs, the FM team is responsible for creating and updating the related Edvin document.

What is the difference between a voucher and an EMD? Voucher is like a "coupon" that the airline issues (either by the helpdesk or via the airline's website), and passengers can redeem it by buying a new ticket, ancillaries, or other services directly from the airline. Whereas EMD, we have when our ticketing team takes a ticket and exchanges its value for a document (EMD) in order to use its value in the future. This means that the customer gets a new EMD ticket number, which contains the original ticket's value. At a later point, when the customer comes back to us with the future flights they want, we take this EMD and reissue it into an electronic ticket. This is the difference with the open ticket, as the latter is actually the customer's ticket. We have removed the segments and added a ghost line to be able to reissue the ticket at a later stage. Open ticket Detailed guideline for Open ticket What is an Open Ticket? With the definition 'Open Ticket', we describe a PNR for which we issued ticket(s), but after the customer's request, we have removed the segments (usually prior to departure) in order to rebook the ticket in the future, within a specific time limit in the validity that the airline sets in their guidelines (always check FM/Travel Alerts/COVID-19 policies). To keep the booking active, we put in a ghost line and remove the flight segments so we will be able to use it later. Keep in mind that what we present to the customer as a "voucher," in reality, is called an Open Ticket because the ticket remains "open" for future use. We can also issue EMD vouchers in GDS if the airline allows it, and you get a number similar to a ticket number (e.g., like a baggage EMD number). Then the customer comes back with this EMD number, and we reissue it into an electronic ticket number (a normal e-ticket). For further information, check below EMD/Voucher. In cases where the voucher is issued by the airline after ETG has asked for it on behalf of the passenger, actions need to be taken by FL and NOT by BO. Such requests are NOT to be queued to BO for handling. Steps to be followed: 1. Phone/Email agent reads the relevant Covid 19 docs and identifies if the voucher is eligible for the specific ticket and if we as an OTA need to request it to the airline on the passenger’s behalf. 2. If yes, inform passengers about the rules of the voucher (validity, new travel, etc). 3. If pax agrees,  put the case on support. 4. Support agents will either send the request to the airline per email or will fill out the necessary online voucher form, depending on each airline’s policy. 5. What should we pay attention to? How to read covid19 and FM travel alert edvin document. When you select one airline, you can see immediately what options are offered by the airline. The options that appear separately are ''Refund'', Rebooking, ''Open tkt'', ''Voucher'' (in the voucher you find more detailed info in regards to if we are talking about voucher or emd). When reading the instructions for one route or one category (e.g. refund for UN flights), you need to read the whole line till the end for additional information. Do not stop at the second point, where you see ‘’Yes’’ or ‘’NO’’. What each category means: Office ID - for which PCC the policy applies 
Affected Travel or Tickets -  for which routes/itinerary the policy applies to 
Refund - is full refund an option? SC date - the date a schedule change happened (for the majority of the airlines, we state ‘’no restrictions’’ as the date that a schedule change happened does not affect the policy) 
Ticket issue date - the date a ticket was issued 
Travel date - for which travel dates the policy applies. If there is at least one bound (OB or IB) of the ticket included in the travel date, then the policy applies, unless stated otherwise 
Deadline - is there a deadline to apply for refund/rebooking/open tkt/voucher/emd 
Endorsement - if there is something to be added in the ENDO BOX. Here we also put waiver codes to be inserted as remarks or OSI.

Please note that when remark (OSI,SSR etc) is required from the airline, we should first add this and then delete the segments. Refund Via - from which system to process refunds 
No show - what happens in case of no-shows. You always need to check No show column. SC Policy Apply - In here we write ‘’YES’’ or ‘’NO’’ and it answers the question ‘’Can we apply the Schedule Policy of the airline in case of UN-TK/UN?’’. Also for later dates than the ones mentioned in the Travel Alert, you follow the schedule change policy normally. Additional Information - Here we write any additional info that needs to be mentioned or how to apply the rebooking/open tkt/voucher/emd policy. Rebooking, Rerouting - YES or NO depending if it’s allowed. New Travel Dates - dates for new travel to be done 
Validity - Check validity column and Ticket validity document. Voucher/EMD Document In the third column, its written if we are talking about an EMD or a Voucher (the expand option always states voucher).

The deadline refers to the deadline for the voucher to be issued. The validity refers till when the passenger can redeem the voucher/utilize the EMD. The new travel dates are for what dates pax can use the voucher/EMD on. In the additional information we include info for 3 things a. how to apply for the voucher/ how to send it for EMD issuance; b. how pax can use the voucher/EMD; c. if the voucher/EMD is refundable or not, and how to proceed. Edvin automatic errands. For all orders that we send out Bulk Emails and customers have accepted the option for Open Ticket, our system will automatically: Delete flight segments (Amadeus and Sabre) Add ghost line (Amadeus and Sabre) Add remarks in GDS (Amadeus and Sabre) So, in Edvin you will see: Order errand that we have sent an email to the customer. Order errand when the customer has answered. If the customer approved the open ticket option, the order status will be updated to “Changed” (for the orders already cancelled, this option cannot be technically updated) Therefore, If you come across a cancelled order where a note is added that the customer accepted the voucher option you can still inform and assist the customer with the open ticket according to set routines in Shelf for a specific airline. Just check if segments are cancelled and ghost line is added.

If you see that the customer accepted this option for open ticket and the order is already on Rebooking Support queue because of a previous request of the customer, we proceed as per his latest confirmation/request. Sometimes you will also see a note in errands regarding a chargeback. When you are handling e-mails and see this information, you should not take any action (do not reply to customer), just close the email and add an errand writing down email number and the name of the person that contacted us, along with his request. The department checking chargebacks will handle it accordingly. If this happens during a call, we tell him that he has started a procedure with his bank and he can get details only through them from now on. We do not proceed with anything else if there is no further info in errands. In case you see the below in Edvin notes:

this means the customer has received a voucher that was issued by the airline company already. Regardless if he has replied to our Bulk email, the customer will need to contact the airline directly if he wants to use the voucher. Usually the segments will also be E/EXCH (exchanged). Important information in GDS. For segments: UN - cancelled TK - alternative UC - unavailable / cancelled HX - no-show / cancelled \* \*check in history when this segment appeared as HX. If it was before departure, it is probably cancelled/changed with the airline directly. If after, then it should be no-show. You can use the commands RHI for Amadeus and \*HI for Sabre. Keep in mind that sometimes you might find PNRs without flight segments, specifically for orders with close departures. Those probably have been removed from our Ticketing department to avoid financial cost (ADMs). You will probably see the following in GDS as an indication of the above (but sometimes it will be a regular ghostline): eg. MIS 1A HK1 STO 04MAR-SEGMENT REMOVED TO AVOID CHARGES You should still proceed as per the FM routines to verify Travel Alerts and assist passengers as per the directions we have there.

Whenever we have a ticket with status R/RFND (refunded) or S/SUSP (suspended) and there are no notes in Edvin confirming such an action was performed on our side, then probably the customer has proceeded with issuing a voucher directly with the airline company. Usually in those cases, there will be a remark in GDS, informing us that we should remove HX segments. So, if you come across such a case, make sure to remove the HX segments from the PNR. To check the validity of the ticket, you should find the fare rules and then open the category  Maximum stay. If nothing is mentioned there, then the validity should be 1 year from the date of ticket issuance. Also, make sure that you check the category Seasonality as there might be restrictions on which date the ticket can be used. If you are to proceed with a change, fill in all the required information in the Register Errand ''Template''. For cancellations, you do not have to place the refund on the queue in GDS, but rather it will be placed in Edvin queue after you go through the Modify order option.

Step 22 VI exceptions As some travel sellers do not operate 24/7, there may be situations where customers are unable to reach them for assistance with the Self Transfer Guarantee product (aka connection guarantee). Additionally, direct assistance to the customer is restricted, and information should only be provided to the travel sellers. To improve the customer experience, an additional alternative, as an exception, has been introduced for VI orders issued via Amadeus B2B (1A). In cases where the customer cannot reach the travel seller in time to request assistance, a 500 EUR cap is applied to Self-Transfer Guarantee bookings. This refund is based on proof of any additional costs incurred by the customer. Check more details about "When the Self Tranfer Guarantee is applicable vs when is not"
[image extracted from Content - 1A Travel Seller (Amadeus) 20250310-071533.pdf page 12: images/ca7f5d4390aabe436898b396a7fedefa69b087f512d24ff595b8799a8efaab83.jpg]

Actions SC VI Agents Should Take: 1. Confirm that the Travel Seller was unable to assist the customer on time. Ensure that the travel seller was unavailable to help the customer within a reasonable timeframe. Check that the new schedule change is close to the original departure time to ensure eligibility for this exceptional process. Confirm if there were more than 24hrs including bank holidays or weekends to determine if the customer was contacting them within their operating period. 2. Request proof from the Travel Seller. Ask the travel seller to provide receipts for any new tickets purchased by the customer to reach their final destination. (Note: A new template will be created for this step.) 3. Review the costs. Ensure that the total amount of the additional costs does not exceed 500 EUR for the entire order (not pe passenger). Ensure that the total additional costs are for the new flights only with original baggage/seating if applicable. Hotels and meals are not covered with this exception. The cost refunded will be up to 500 EUR. If the new ticket(s) value is lower, then we will refund the new tickets. When the new value exceeds 500 EUR, then only 500 EUR will be refunded. The new flight should be the same calendar day or -/+ 1 day from the original departure. 4. Modify the button in Edvinю Update the Modify button in the Edvin system to allow the payout team to process the refund to the travel seller for the eligible amount.

By following these steps, agents can effectively handle cases where customers are unable to reach the travel seller promptly, ensuring that refunds are processed accurately while maintaining a positive customer experience for B2B customers. Live chat through Genesys provides the option to offer customers immediate assistance. Routines and workflows for Chat are as per normal processes. No phone calls will be received during the chat task. If you receive 1 chat interaction and 1 email interaction → reply to the chat first. If you receive 2 chat interactions → priority to the first chat. Maximum 5 minute hold time 
Automatic 2 minutes ACW time after the disconnection of chat,once 2 minutes have passed next interaction will be received (Live on 01April2023) 
Always offer an alternative option when the customer's initial request is not possible - when applicable Some examples... - Customer chats to cancel their flight due to FM but we have no TA policy. Offer cancellation as per fare rules as an alternative - Customer needs a naco/nach but it is not allowed on the ticket. Offer cancellation as per fare rules if the ticket is refundable and book a new ticket - Customer wants to cancel their booking due to FM, but the ticket is non-refundable, check the TA on if an open ticket or a voucher option can be offered Step 8 Idle time and disconnect Scenario 1 At the initial stage of the conversation, the customer remains idle. The flow goes as follows: 
2 minutes idle customer you send → Customer doesn't respond 1st Warning ETG/B.com UK 3 minutes later you send Close chat after no response for 5 min ETG/B.com UK And then disconnect.

Total idle time for customers =5 minutes Scenario 2 The conversation has started, we have shared a few pieces of information with the customer, and all of a sudden the customer is idle. For example, for a rebooking request, we do the pricing and ask the customer if he/she is interested in paying. Or cancellation requests, we share the penalties and ask the customers for confirmation to proceed. And the customer rests idle. The flow goes as follows: Agent asks if the customer wishes to proceed with the next action or waiting for a reaction from the customer. The customer remains idle. 2 minutes idle customer you send → Customer doesn't respond 1st Warning ETG/B.com UK 
3 minutes later you send →  Close chat after no response for 5 min ETG/B.com UK And then disconnect. Note:  If the agent does not come back to the customer within 3 minutes (as stated in the 1st warning script) the agent can delay a maximum of 5 minutes to send the “No response for 5 minutes” script. The maximum acceptable total idle time of customer  is 7 minutes. Scenario 3 The request has been replied to(for example. rebooking completed/cancellation completed), everything is done and the customer remains idle. Agent shares the chat script '' Question before closing ETG/B.com UK''. 3 minutes later you send Close chat after no response for 5 min ETG/B.com UK And then disconnect. Total idle time of customer 3 minutes. After the disconnection, the customer can no longer reply to the same thread

Replying to interactions PagelastupdatedonJanuary24 2025 Chat scripts are available in Genesys and it is mandatory to use Genesys canned responses while responding to the customers. Scripts can be also found here. Always start the reply by introducing yourself. When receiving a transferred interaction the second agent should use the script titled [Chat] Chat Opening (asking to wait) ETG/B.com UK '''Hello, {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, my name is <Agent First Name> Please give me a moment to review your request.'' There is no need to ask again the customer what is his/her request. The agent can retrieve the details of the request that was stated to the first agents,  via Genesys or via the communication tab in Edvin. Wrap-ups to be used as per normal routines. In case of SC request, redirect the customer interaction to the Schedule change Chat queue. In case of a CR request, redirect the customer to our contact form for CR claims. The agents need to reply to the interaction within 1 min and if there is any delay in replying to the customer then there will be a markdown from QA 
While handling the chat interaction always remember to check the communication dashboard in Edvin and close any dupe/already handled emails/chat interactions. Do not use shortenings. Please verify if the customer has already inserted the desired flights using the Self Service Rebooking link here. There is no need to request the flights again.

paragraph: Step by step In case you want to rebook an OOS order and ATC is not working, check the manual rebooking guidelines. Also, you may find detailed steps below: The recalculation must be based on the lowest applicable historical fare in the highest originally ticketed booking class (RBD) and fare family per direction of the remaining flight coupons. This means: using applicable historical fare for the same or higher RBD in the original fare family for remaining coupons in the direction of travel. In case no fare is available in the required RBD of the original fare family: use fare in higher RBD and/or higher fare family. Change to a lower RBD/ fare family is not permitted. Observe all fare rules of the new fare including Advance Purchase (ADVP) at the time of ticketing of the original ticket (historical calculation). Use the complete value of the original ticket as a credit towards the new ticket. In case the new price is lower than the old price, the difference to the original fare/taxes including unused YQ may be credited via residual value EMD regardless of fare type. DCC (YR) remains nonrefundable. If the passenger had purchased ancillary services on the skipped coupons, such EMDs are nonrefundable. If currency conversion is needed, use the Bankers Selling Rate (BSR) applicable at the time of the origina ticket issue date.

If Original Travel is within or Less than 4 Hours: Follow the standard refund routine as usual. When handling normal cancellations such as refunds according to ticket rules, 24-hour cancellation, void and taxes, etc. we always use Auto refund. Never change to manual unless you have a waiver or authorization or you have been given direct instructions by the airline. In the automated refund function the penalty field, the used fare, and the refund fields are always greyed out and not able to be edited. NEVER refund a ticket if the refunded amount is 0. If a ticket is fully non-refundable, you should only cancel the segments in Farelogix, and not follow the refund steps per ticket. paragraph: Void: EMD is automatically refunded when you refund the ticket, do not try to refund the EMD separately. Fare rule: EMD is almost always non-refundable according to the ticket rule if nothing else is stated. If the EMD would be refundable then it has to be refunded via the BSP link. The ticket is to be refunded in Sprk as usual, then copy the EMD number and add it in Edvin in "Other note to BO" and please write "Send RA via BSP link for the EMD: XXXXX, tickets already refunded in Sprk". Taxes: EMD is non-refundable. Force majeure: EMD has to be refunded via the BSP link. There is no guarantee for an EMD refund. Each ticket is to be refunded in Sprk as usual (if Force majeure info doesn't state anything else for the specific situation), then copy the EMD number and add in Edvin in "Other note to BO" and write: "Please end RA via BSP link for the EMD: XXXXX". Please see the additional steps below for FL to complete. Schedule change: EMD has to be refunded via the BSP link. There is no guarantee for an EMD refund. Each ticket is to be refunded in Sprk as usual (if LHG policy or the agent from LHG hasn't stated anything else for the specific situation). Voluntary cancellation after the voluntary exchange: If the customer wants to cancel by the rules after a voluntary change has been finalized, the refund will be by the rules (automated calculation by FAST). Voluntary cancellation after the involuntary exchange: At the moment this is not supported by FAST. Please escalate this to SL in order to raise a refund application via BSP. GDPR General info: In case of GDPR reasons, the passenger might be eligible for the refund. If ticket rules do not allow voluntary refund, it needs to be done via BSP refund application (it will be requested by SL team). Medical certificates need to be included with the application. Who is ADR? Aeroporti di Roma (abbreviated ADR) is an Italian fixed-base operator of Leonardo da Vinci-Fiumicino Airpor (FCO)  and Rome Ciampino Airport (CIA). The aim of the cooperation with this partner is to promote longer stop-overs in Rome. The initiative has received a lot of attention from the Rome Mayorship and also from the Italian Ministry of Tourism. Partner’s website: https://www.adr.it/web/aeroporti-di-roma-en/ General info about ETG - ADR cooperation Live date of the partnership: Markets: The partnership starts with below markets: Italian market served via IT website German market served via DE website rest of European markets served via IE website UK market served via UK website USA market served via US website Canadian market served via CA website Booking flow & branding: ADR customers will complete the booking process on whitelisted sites branded as Flyandvisitrome, i.e: ie.flyandvisitrome.com it.flyandvisitrome.com uk.flyandvisitrome.com us.flyandvisitrome.com de.flyandvisitrome.com ca.flyandvisitrome.com

ADR will be live on Metasearch engines with content focusing on trips with stopovers in Rome from all relevant geographies (mostly VI content). Payments: ETG is MoR of all transactions, meaning that the charge that the customer sees on his bank account is from ETG. Post-booking handling: All the booking inquiries are handled by ETG as per standard ETG processes. Disability assistance FL Phone/Chat Process When a customer calls, or chats requesting wheelchair assistance, follow these steps: 1.

Inform Customer About Online Consent: Inform the customer about the process for completing the online contact form to provide consent for handling their sensitive data, and managing their assistance request. 2. Send Assistance Consent Email: Use the "Assistance Consent" email template from Edvin. Send the email to the customer. They will receive a link directing them to our contact form.

The customer must click "Write to Customer Service" to create an email, write their request, and check the consent box. 3. If Consent is Given During Phone/Chat: Stay on the call/chat until the request is completed. Request the customer to provide an Etrack number and verify that consent is marked as TRUE. Use the newly created Etrack category “FL ASSISTANCE CONSENT” for this task. This category will allow us to receive customer consent emails. Proceed with the request as usual. 4. Once Consent is Received: Add the wheelchair assistance request to the booking. Once the request is confirmed, inform the customer over the phone/chat. Send an email confirmation using the “Assistance Request-Conf.” template in Edvin. Ensure you close the Etrack case by clicking on "Close Case." 5. If Unable to Confirm Assistance: Place the case in the support queue and advise the customer to wait. Mention the error that occurred and the priority of the request in the errands: High Priority (To be handled in 12 hours): "Departure within 7 days – follow up within 12 hours." Medium Priority (To be handled in 24 hours): "Departure more than 7 days away – follow up within 24 hours." 6. Waiting or no response on Phone/Chat: If waiting for consent during a call or chat, allow up to 5 minutes for a response, as per the standard hold process. Close the interaction after giving a final warning if the customer does not respond within this timeframe, as per the standard process.

\*Remember not to mention sickness or wheelchair in Edvin. Assistance requested and confirmed/ not confirmed is ok to write. FL Support Process 1. Try to confirm the request: First FL support agent will try to confirm the request on the GDS/Portal. 2. Contact Airline to Confirm the Request: If unable to confirm the request on GDS/Portal then FL support agent will contact the airline to confirm the assistance request. Once confirmed, send an email confirmation to the customer using the “Assistance Request-Conf.” template in Edvin. 3. If Unable to Confirm assistance request: If the request cannot be confirmed with the airline, contact the customer via phone. If the customer cannot be reached, send an email using the “Unconfirmed Assistance Request” template in Edvin.

The email has a link to a specific form on the website where the customer can upload the certificate and leave his consent. The FL agent shall complete the cancellation, send an email confirmation of the cancellation from Edvin using the template for cancellation protection, and change the email to category 160.7 reply with the template ”GDPR - medical certificate”. Step 2 General Information All agents are expected to check the communication hub while handling emails and close any already handled/dupe interactions. Email cases/Interactions pushed to the agent; no manual picking from queues. Emails and phone calls are treated and measured the same way - as Interactions. Always insert a retention line/ghost line when the customer contacts us for any request, if not already inserted. If it is a Multi PNR and we only handle the LCC booking/ Portal booking, we still need to add a Ghostline in the GDS PNR. One queue for all channels; no specific email queue.

Agents will receive a mix of phone and email interactions unless skills are changed on the agent level. Genesys detects language from text and routes it to the corresponding queue. Edvin API will give higher priority to orders with departure within 3 days. 1 active email interaction at a time. Agents will place email interactions on Edvin support when a case needs further investigation, but email always needs to be responded to with the correct template. No internal recategorization. Cases that need handling by our Schedule Change department will be transferred to the Schedule Change Queues accordingly, the same way as we do with phone call interactions. See below for more details on the SC transferring. The time displayed is the local time of the agent. Always reply in English if the customer has written in English no matter what market he/she has booked on. Always offer an alternative option when the customer's initial request is not possible - when applicable. Someexamples: - Customer emails to cancel their flight due to FM but we have no TA policy. Offer cancellation as per fare rules as an alternative. - Customer needs a naco/nach but it is not allowed on the ticket. Offer cancellation as per fare rules if th ticket is refundable and book a new ticket. - Customer emails to cancel their booking due to FM, but the ticket is non-refundable, check the TA on if an open ticket or a voucher option can be offered.

Step 6 General process UPDATE: Seating fulfillment (seating light/ map & besides) has started since on February 2023 for LCC carriers through Travelfusion and Tripstact. Gordian is a new partner that will try to fulfill the bag and seats that could not be automatically  issued by the system and they have fallen to our Manual queues. In version 1, we will start with the luggage and only a few sites until we make sure everything goes as expected. Target group  : Gordian will undertake the fulfillment for the LCC carriers and VI bookings (GDS + LCC). NDC carriers (portals) are excluded. Due to some restrictions, Gordian will fulfill the luggage for specific carriers either for GDS or for LCC. With 21APR22 as an expected starting date, Gordian will fulfill the luggage for VI orders before ending up in the Manual queue in Edvin. If they fail, the order will be automatically placed in the Manual queue. For pure LCC orders, fulfillment will be executed by Gordian if the system fails and can not issue the bag. If Gordian also fails the order will be automatically placed in the Manual queue, at which point agents will take over. Associated queues : "LCC Ancillary" and manual queues of VI. Those queues are handled by the SL. - The SLA will be 3 hours.

When the luggage is successfully completed, an indication appears in Edvin indicating for which PN the luggage was added and for which segments. - We do not send orders to Gordian where the departure is within 12 hours.

They will either try to reach out to the airline, so the emd will be re-associated, otherwise they will issue a new emd with a charge on us. If the emd is not visible, leave a comment to the ticketing team “ Pls issue a new bag emd for this customer” b) Refund old emd and issue new according to the airline's rules. - In phase 1 we cannot claim any refund from Gordian for the emd for the rebooking process. This is applicable only for the cancellation process. - Leave a note to the Ticketing team “Pls issue a new bag emd for this customer”

If not, check on Manage my booking manually re-associate the baggage ancillary.

FAQ 1. When a customer is contacting because of baggage not being added by Gordian, what should the FL agent do? This cooperation is something between us and Gordian. Gordian has an SLA 3 hours of baggage fulfillment. If they are not able to add the bag, the order will be automatically placed to our Manual queues where SL is handling. That means that if the customer calls because the bag has not been added yet, the FL agents will see that the order is on our Manual queues and they will inform the customer to wait. Nothing changes to our routines. 2. Since Gordian does not send any confirmations to the customer, will we(Second Line) send a confirmation once the baggage is added? We have maintained the same flow. When a customer makes a booking on our website and purchases a bag, the confirmation email states 1 piece of bag. If the system cannot issue the bag and the order falls to our manual queue, the SL agents issue a bag without sending any further confirmation because the customer did not know that the bag was not issued automatically. SL agents are sending email to customers when they are not able to issue the bag. 3. Which team in Second Line will be responsible for communication with Gordian if any clarifications will be needed? Payouts and Claims have access to Gordian’s portal, so if they want to check for example the status of the bag or if the efund has been received, they will log-in to Gordian’s portal. 4.

If Gordian will issue an EMD for a GDS reservation but it will not be visible in GDS and the customer will ask for a confirmation or EMD number, what FL agent should do? The confirmation email states that the bag has been added, so as soon as the FL agents will see the respective indication in Edvin that the bag has been added by Gordian it is guaranteed. This case is very rare because the customers do not know that we are issuing emds. 5. In the General process it is mentioned that Gordian will fulfill the luggage for specific carriers either for GDS or for LCC. For which carriers exactly the baggage may be added? This is not something that affects the FL agents because this project is being tested a lot.To point out again that SLA is only 3 hours, if Gordian fails the order will be automatically placed on our queues, so FL agents will see that the bag is in progress.

You can proceed with ''Modify order'' and '' Ancillary -Voluntary'' reasons choosing the specific product to be refunded. If a customer contacts us before departure asking about baggage, and the FL agent can see that it has not been added while purchased, take action and make sure it is added, to avoid any issues for the customer at the airport. Before you redirect a customer to the specific contact form to raise a claim, follow the below checklist. 1. Baggage/seating was purchased by the customer as separate add on or baggage is  included in the ticket, and is stated in the order confirmation or travel document but not added by ETG. The customer was forced to buy baggage or seating at the airport and can provide proof -the invoice. 2. Check if the order is affected by any known baggage issues stated here, if yes-follow the guidelines stated in the link, if no-follow the below guidelines depending on the channel of interaction.

paragraph: Step 6 Baggage Claim Scenarios If a customer contacts us before departure asking about baggage, and the FL agent can see that it has not been added while purchased, take action and make sure it is added, to avoid any issues for the customer at the airport. Only if the trip has been completed and the customer purchased baggage directly with the airline should we redirect the customer to raise a claim for baggage. Below you will find the most common baggage claims scenarios.

pdf_name: Content - How to redirect baggage and seating claims 20250310-073224.pdf
paragraph: 1. Baggage is shown as included in the ticket during the booking process on the website The order confirmation email states baggage is included, but not stated in the travel document. Ticket when opened on GDS/airlines website or in the portal does not include baggage, no EMD for baggage has been issued. 2. Baggage is shown as included in the ticket during the booking process on the website. Baggage allowance in order confirmation and travel document shows that baggage is included. Ticket when opened on GDS/airlines website or in the portal does not include baggage, no EMD for baggage has been issued. 3. The baggage was purchased as an add-on and the ticket should have been upgraded to fare including baggage. The ticket has not been upgraded due to an error and remained with zero bag allowance. Order confirmation and travel document state baggage is included. The ticket when opened in GDS has zero bag allowance and no EMD has been issued. 4. Baggage was purchased as an add-on. Due to an error, baggage was not added as an EMD or as an additional service for LCC carriers. The order confirmation email states baggage is included and the travel document has no baggage allowance stated. 5. Wrong information regarding baggage allowance or dimensions was provided in the order confirmation or travel document, the customer had to pay directly to the carrier for extra kg or size baggage due to incorrect information provided by ETG. 6.

Outsourcing Support Welcome! You can raise a Outsourcing Support request from the options provided What can we help you with? All requests regarding Frontline If passenger is at the airport and SC has happened more than 24H before departure and passengers have not received any information. Below you can find the different types of requests: FLsup ort Authority / Reason Code:  Reason code for a possible charge or waive our involuntary service fee. (For human/tech errors make sure to check also here). Technical Issue: System Error / Technical Issue. Fare hike: We have a technical issue with the information not showing clearly when there is a fare hike. The hike will always be there, but the customer should have received a pop-up about the same and got an updated payment page with the new price. This needs to be checked with SO/TL, for a possible charge. Guidelines: General information about our procedures and guidelines for case handling. Password Reset:  Reset the password (Portals, Edvin, etc.) 
Pending Provider Booking: Booking with status ''Pending or Shopping'' that needs to be checked with ticketing or LCC agents. Refund Issue: Refund application status or cancellation procedure. Update Information: Update / re-phrase guidelines, instructions, blog post, along with any relevant policies received in communication with YY/consolidator (FM policies or Edvin docs related info).

paragraph: SCSup ort Travel within 24 hours: When the original travel departure is within 24 hours, and we fail to handle the request on time, so urgent in-house assistance is required. Note: If the passenger is over the phone/chat and the departure is within 24 hours, the interaction has to be transferred to the respective queue on Genesys. VAN card issuance request:  When a VAN card issuance is required. OUT partners do not have access to create one. ETG Escalation: Request raised from a specific support task ETG Escalation. Guidelines: Provide assistance and guidelines about different types of requests, such as Shelf content, Airline policy from Edvin, Password Reset, and/ or Tech Error assistance. Refund Issues: Refund application status or cancellation procedure. Update Information: Redirect the request to another department about different types of requests, such as Shelf content or Airline policy from Edvin to be updated, Tech Error which might affect different departments. Mishandling: When an internal mishandling occurs and in-house assistance for resolution is required. Authority/ Reason code: Provide authorization to proceed with an internal or airline flow and/or policy or reason code for an error is required. Farelogix: Farelogix cases related to SC and handled end-to-end.

paragraph: When to use MOTO Payment MOTO is a preferred method of payment for all products and services as well as for collecting our handling fees. MOTO should always be suggested as the first payment option during phone interactions unless it is not technically supported. (The MOTO Payment button will not be available in Edvin when creating an Add on cart for orders, where the MOTO form of payment is not technically supported). Note1: MOTO Payment is NOT supported for LATAM markets. It will not be available as a payment the Add on cart in Edvin for these markets. Note 2: All cards are supported for payments via MOTO, except Maestro cards, which will NOT be accepted on AU on the CA market. Note 3: that MOTO payment will not be technically possible when active monitoring is in place (such as Supervisor monitoring or other agent shadowing). Booking.com orders are no longer excluded from the MOTO Payment option. For markets, where MOTO is enabled, you shall always first suggest MOTO Payment as available payment method also on Booking.com orders. Never send the customer to secure payment flow via Genesys, if MOTO Payment is not available as an option in Ad oncart! Genesys is not able to differentiate the markets, for which MOTO payment is not supported. Of course, for all requests, if the customer is not able to fulfill the payment on the spot, during the initial phone call or denies processing via MOTO, you may still offer a Payment link as per standard routines.

pdf_name: Content - Payment methods for post-sale services 20250310-074043.pdf
paragraph: Whenever you offer a Payment link, you shall state in your errand the reason why you could not use MOTO (i.e, pax denied MOTO, MOTO not enabled etc.). Support agents should also use the MOTO Payment as a preferred method of fulfilling the charges during their outgoing phone interactions. For details on how to make an outbound call, please refer to the relevant section here. Please note that the option to send the customer to IVR flow will be available only if the call is performed on behalf of a relevant queue. Schedule change requests shall be handled as per separate guidelines. For more detailed information, check 4)Schedulechange handling page section. REMINDER: Always respect the deadline required for handling by other departments, as per standard routines: For rebooking cases, the reissue request must be placed on the respective queue at least 4 hours before the original departure and/or at least 6 hours before the new flight. Otherwise, changes are not possible. For ancillary requests, the request can be handled up to 48h prior to the departure. For all other services, the request can be handled up to 24h prior to the departure.

paragraph: How to handle a MOTO Payment - step by step If for any reason, at any stage of the below flow, the call will involuntarily drop, you are obliged to call the customer back, following the standard routine for dropped calls. Please note that the option to send the customer to IVR flow will be availab only if you start a new interaction in Genesys on behalf of the relevant queue. For more information click here. 1. Kindly ask the customer to prepare the card, which he/she will use for the payment. 2. In Edvin, create an Ad oncart as per standard routines and click on the blue ‘MOTOpayment’ button, at the bottom of the created cart: 3. The below window will pop-up: 4. Reconfirm with the customer all the details of the requested amendments and the final cost along with its breakdown (the cost of all added products/services need to be specified separately along with the total cost). The customer does NOT have a visual summary of the additional service he/she is purchasing. Verbal reconfirmation of the cost breakdown and the details of the amendmen ore redirecting the customer to the payment flow is mandatory to avoid mishandlings! 5. Leave Edvin and open your on-going phone interaction in Genesys. 6. Inform the customer that they will be redirected to the automatic secure payment flow, where an IVR message will ask him/her to insert the card number (16 digits), the card expiration date (in MM/YY format) and CVV code (card verification value - visible at the back of the card).

pdf_name: Content - Payment methods for post-sale services 20250310-074043.pdf
paragraph: The customer will have a restricted time frame to insert each data (30s for credit card number and 10s for expiration date and CVV each). This information is for your knowledge, you don’t have to communicate it to the customer. If data is inserted incorrectly or not within the stated time frame, the customer will be able to retry the automatic flow up to three times for each category failure or will be able to choose to be redirected back to the agent. 7. In Genesys use the red button ‘SendcustomertosecurePaymentIVR’  under SecurePaymentIVR section on the main screen of your on-going interaction:

In some cases, you will receive the successful payment, but you won’t be able to fulfill the customer’s request on the spot. Such scenarios may be divided into two categories: A. The availability or the cost of the service/ancillary has changed Scenarios including, but not limited to: For rebooking requests: booking class availability change, selected flights not applicable anymore 
For ancillary requests: chosen ancillary not available anymore How to handle such cases? 1. First, check if the service/ancillary is available and can thereby later be saved and confirmed. 2. If the same service is no longer available at the cost initially given to the passenger, inform the passenger that the availability has changed and advise that an additional cost is required in order to fulfil the requests. If the customer agrees to cover the additional charge: Create a new Add-on cart for the remaining cost, confirm that the customer agrees to MOTO Payment and proceed with the payment as per general flow. Do NOT suggest the Payment link method in such cases, as it increases the risk of losing the availability again. If the customer declines to cover the additional charge and demands a refund of the initial add on payment: Follow standard routines for refunds of service that has not been provided. More details can be found here.

pdf_name: Content - Payment methods for post-sale services 20250310-074043.pdf
paragraph:
If the customer declines to cover the additional charge and asks to be provided alternative service within the cost already paid: Suggest an available alternative (a different flight connection, a different seat number etc.) and if accepted, fulfil the actions as per standard routines. 3. If the same service can not be saved: Suggest an available alternative (a different flight connection, a different seat number etc.) If the customer doesn’t accept the proposed alternative, follow standard routines for refunds of service that has not been provided. More details can be found here. B. The request can not be practically fulfilled Scenarios include, but are not limited to: Technical errors 
Requests requiring Support actions (for example rebooking scenarios, name correction) 
Not able to finalize rebooking requests on the airline's website or a VAN card cannot be created 
How to handle such cases? 1. First, check if the service/ancillary can be saved and confirmed by the provider.

pdf_name: Content - Payment methods for post-sale services 20250310-074043.pdf
paragraph: 2. If the service/ancillary can be saved, but you can not finalize the request either due to lack of confirmation from the provider or due to the fact that Support actions need to be taken, inform the passenger that you will forward the request to another department for handling. 3. If the request cannot be finalized on the airline's website (for Portals or LCC handling) or VAN cannot be created: Place the order manually on the Support Queue as per the standard routine here. ATT: MOTO Payments do not end up manually on the Payment Dashboard. If you don’t place the order on the relevant Support Queue manually as per the routine here, the order will remain unhandled! Attention! If you encounter any issue with VAN creation, it is important that you need to follow the routine here. This means that first you need to place the order on Support and the Support agent will raise a System Support Jira for VAN creation. 3. If the same service can not be saved: Suggest an available alternative (a different flight connection, a different seat number etc.) If the customer doesn’t accept the proposed alternative, follow standard routines for refunds of service that has not been provided. More details can be found here. Step 12 Parent step: 4 What is a Payment Link and when to use? What is it? A payment link is a form of payment, which allows the customer to fulfill the payment outside of the call interaction.

pdf_name: Content - Payment methods for post-sale services 20250310-074043.pdf
paragraph:
The agent sets the time frame for which the payment link will be active and sends the secure payment link directly to the customer’s contact email. The agent is not handling any sensitive data, all the card details are inserted by the customer directly to the secure payment link. Once the payment is fulfilled, the payment link ends up in the Support dashboard When to use? A payment link is not a preferred payment method and should not be used as a first option. It can be used for the below scenarios: for requests received via phone interaction, where customer could not proceed with the payment on the spot Due to errors during the payment flow Due to customer’s decision (e.g. customer does not have the payment card handy, declines processing via MOTO) ATT: MOTO should always be suggested as the first payment option. Payment link can be alternatively sent only if the above conditions are met and there is sufficient availability and remaining time before the scheduled departure! for requests received via email interaction, which you are allowed to handle via email as per standard routines 
for all requests for LATAM market orders as MOTO is not supported for those markets 
for request from AU and CA market if the customer can use only Maestro card (if any other card - refer to MOTO) 
during calls when active monitoring is in place (such as Supervisor monitoring or other agent shadow

paragraph: when the customer wants to think or discuss about it before proceeding to the payment. This way, a possible second contact for the same reason might be avoide Please note, that whenever you offer a Payment link, you shall state in your errand the reason why you could not use MOTO (i.e: pax denied MOTO, MOTO not enabled etc.). If MOTO is not available on a particular order or the customer declines using MOTO, but still wishes to proceed with the payment on the spot and during the phone call, you should wait on the line until the payment is processed and handle the paid request accordingly. Otherwise, you have to inform the customer that the price and availability are not guaranteed. The last payment date/time shall be set as described below for each type of request: For rebooking cases, the last payment date/time for Payment link shall be set for 30 minutes (in exceptional cases, when you have sufficient availability and when passenger clearly asks for longer time, you may set the Payment link for maximum 1 hour). The deadline of last valid time for Payment Link  should be 16:30 local time for both ATH/UPA. REMINDER: The reissue request must be placed on the respective queue at least 4 hours before the original departure and/or at least 6 hours before the new flight. Otherwise, changes are not possible.

pdf_name: Content - Payment methods for post-sale services 20250310-074043.pdf
paragraph: For ancillary cases, the last payment date/time for the Payment link can be set for maximum 48 hours from the moment of sending the link, as long as this time frame is not passing the 48 hour before the departure. For all other cases, the last payment date/time for a Payment link can be set for maximum 24 hours from the moment of sending the link, as long as this time frame is not passing the 48 hour before the departure. NOTE: If you handle an order with scheduled departure within the next 48h and the request requires additional payment, you should always proceed via MOTO Payment method. DO NOT send Payment Link for such cases, unless the case falls under scenarios where MOTO can not be supported. Schedule change requests shall be handled as per separate guidelines. For more detailed information check 4) Schedule change handling page in this decision tree. Step 13 Parent step: 4 How to handle a Payment Link - step by step 1. Void/ 24h cancellation rule/ voluntary cancellation/ dupe/ GDPR In general, Void and 24 hour cancellation rule are not allowed according to Ryanair policy. In case the customer has proceeded with a void or 24h cancellation on their own directly with the airline (either on the website of the carrier or through direct contact), it will not be reflected in the portal. So in case you receive a request, where the customer claims they have already requested a refund from the airline, you need to submit a refund request through the portal in order for the consolidator to refund us so that we can process the payout of the amount. For a voluntary cancellation, Ryanair has a general non refundable ticket policy so we cannot make any claim on our own. In case the customer has proceeded with a cancellation according to fare rules on their own directly with the airline (either on the website of the carrier or through direct contact), it will not be reflected in the portal. So in case you receive a request, where the customer claims they have already requested a refund from the airline, you need to submit a refund request through the portal in order for the consolidator to refund us so that we can process the payout of the amount. In general it is not possible for us to claim a refund due to dupe or due to GDPR when it comes to Ryanair.

In case the customer has made the claim on his own directly with the airline, you are required to submit the request through the portal as per the voluntary cancellation. For all the voluntary cancellation scenarios above, please follow the instructions here for void and here for voluntary cancellation in order to claim the refund from FR24, in case the customer has reached out saying that the airline has been contacted and they begun the refund process to the account used for the PNR creation. paragraph: Voluntary and involuntary changes for British Airways booked through Tripstack can now be performed through Edvin without logging in the IAG portal. The same applies for SQ. Applies for: Rebooking for all the passengers Bookings without ancillaries related with seating and baggage For all the other scenarios (split pnr and bookings with baggage or seating ) the process remains manual by logging in the IAG portal or SQ Agent 360 portal - Tripstack for SQ orders.

pdf_name: Content - Post Booking Automation in Edvin for Tripstack changes of BA & SQ (PBA) 20250310-083737.pdf
paragraph:
FAQ (for BA orders):
(ers)
Can we rebook a booking order that includes ancillaries?No,the automation works for bookings without ancillaries related to seating and baggage.For all the other scenarios (split pnr and bookings with baggage or seating ) the process remains manual by logging in to the IAG portal.
Can we rebook 1 out of X amount of passengers?No,as the rebooking automation applies to all passengers in the booking.
If the ticket is already partially used or reissued,can we still proceed?This is supported by BA, however,this cannot be processed via automation.The process remains manual by logging in to the IAG portal.
Is there a time limit on how close to departure you can use it?No,technically there isn't.
Can we resend the new ticket confirmation to a different e-mail address?Kindly copy the information from the Communication tab and send it via Edvin's blank template email.
What happens if there is a technical issue and the payment fails? Do we get an option to collect the payment again,does this affect the rebooking,and/or if the rebooking is completed through Edvin and the payment was not successful what will be the next action?Rebooking won't go through,and the process will have to start over.

FEEDER FLIGHTS - When in a long international connection, there is a short flight within the same region operated by another airline than the operating carrier - this regional connection is called a feeder flight. If you can not receive pricing by using any of the suggested manual pricing commands it may mean that the chosen booking class on the feeder flight is not compatible with the fare basis of the original ticket.

If you need to check which booking class shall be used for feeder flights for a specific fare basis, type in FQS01/ABA (01 for fare line number one from the list after FQD command, /ABA for airline code - British Airways operating the feeder flight). UPGRADE – Ticket is normally possible to upgrade if it doesn’t state in rule that it is not permitted. A basic rule is to only take published to published and unpublished to unpublished fare. PUBLISHED/UNPUBLISHED – Almost never possible to upgrade from unpublished to published. Exceptions exist. Never permitted to downgrade from published to unpublished. AP – No need to check if outbound flown on a roundtrip ticket. Complaint for SC support being only in English: You can advise we are doing the best we can to assist and due to the big workload such requests currently are handled in English language. Issues with airline locators: Once the confirmation email is received the majority of passengers do not know how to use it or they have difficulties with the airlines website to retrieve their bookings. Most of the cases with this issue appear to be with GOL (G3). Please remember to share PNRs in private message. Try to handle the case end-to-end. If call back is required, you need to contact the customer. If no reply by the first call you can send email from edvin. You can reply to the review as well. Contact airline for some requests.

If the request is placed on support and it is something that can be handled from the agent assigned on this task, you may proceed with the handling and remove it from the support queue, otherwise you may inform the passenger that this request is more demanding and our support team is checking it and they will be informed eventually. Refund delays:  The escalation to SL through RD has the same priority as all the other requests. In case you are facing a more demanding case, you can escalate it to your Manager/ Team Leader/ Supervisor/ FL Coordinator. For rebooking requests we do not reply through the platform nor we send email to the customer, unless we have contacted them through outbound call and they are aware that we will be sending them a payment link. On each complaint we provide only one reply to the customer even if they reply back, we do not continue the thread.

Step 5 Parent step: 1 QA Methodology to follow Pasengers 1. Never force the passengers to pay extra for the losses we have incurred due to our agent error. Yes, certainly we can try to convince them & give alternate options that will reduce our losses 
2. ETG purely believes in customer service & we have to be loyal with our customers, remember the ETG value and try to create a sense of urgency for us to be able to conclude our findings. 3. Be natural & try to not use scripts, always keep initiating small talks, building rapport with the customers will help us gain the trust, it’s not important that we have to save the complete loss, even partial savings are better than to lose the customer. 4. Make sure to explain to the customer that you are well versed with the products & very knowledgeable. Establishing and maintaining a deep personal connection with your customers is highly important. Often, it can be one of the key factors that will drive better! 5. Make clear errand notes with detailed information, as we don’t have run behind handling time, our core task is saving the retail losses. 6.

The Ghostline in Sabre will keep the PNR alive for 180 days (6 months) from the last active segment in the ticket or if there are no segments from the day the retention line is inserted. Please note that ghostlines expire after 6 months, therefore, even if the customer is asking for refund updates or to use his open ticket, you need to check if the PNR is active. Ghostlines can be removed from the PNRs in the same way as the segments, so please keep in mind that if the ghostline in a particular PNR has a close expiration date, you have to remove the old one and add the new one.
