Selfservice Rebooking description From mid-April, we have started sending bulk emails to our customers asking them to convert their tickets to open / voucher. Right now we have received more than 150.000 PNR that have accepted the voucher solution. Through the self-service rebooking option, passengers will be able to select their new flights on their own. Customers will receive their voucher code via e-mail along with the instructions they need to follow in order to rebook their ticket(s). \*\*Apr 2, 2021\*\* As some airlines have extended the deadline for open ticket rebooking, we are re-sending vouchers to customers or updating the validity of the existing ones. So far, approximately 20.000 vouchers have been resent for Lufthansa Group as well as KLM / Air France, and more will follow. The information of the sent message, as well as the restrictions, can be seen in the relevant errand note: Image failed to load(https://wiki.etraveli.net/download/attachments/110899194/image2021-4-2_9-32- 20.png?version=1&modificationDate=1617345140000&api=v2) The instructions provided to the customers are the same as the ones we have received from each carrier that provides the open ticket option and we have sent the bulk e-mail. In the received e-mail, a link will be included that will redirect the customers in our booking flow in order to select their new flights, insert travel details and proceed with payment.

The customer will insert the voucher code in the respective field as you can see below before the payment: The voucher amount will be deducted from the price the customer will have to pay and after the payment, we will try to reissue the ticket manually from our side.

IRREGULARITY AND SCHEDULE CHANGE PROCEDURES If the passenger has been placed on an alternative flight by TAP, he can make a free amendment to another flight/connecting flight he considers acceptable – any additional change will be subject to fare conditions. Note: The travel agent is required to notify all ticketed and confirmed passengers of any schedule change or flight cancellation immediately after receiving notice. This free booking change must be processed within 10 days after the schedule change (UN/TK sent to the PNR).

Any rebooking made or requested after the period of 10 days of the schedule change may be considered a voluntary booking change, according to fare conditions. Changes of origin and/or destination for regular schedule changes are not allowed. In case of an exceptional situation, for example, the closure of the airport, etc., specific rules shall apply and will be divulged by TAP. If no alternative TP operated flight is available, you can rebook to a TP marketing flight (TP flight number but operated by another airline) following the same rules described above. Tickets to/from/via Russia with Russian airlines: Some customers refer to Russian law for a refund of their flight tickets in medical and/or death situations. If the airline refund the passenger we should do the same. We are however not obliged to refund the passenger and take the cost for such refund. 
The backoffice refunds team will send a Refund Application (RA) to the airline, attaching the medical/death certificate. This is regardless if there is a waiver in the fare rules or not. We as a travel agency will have no impact on the airline's decision to grant or decline the refund application or not, therefore no refund should be promised to the customer when cancelling. Important Note: For U6-Ural Airlines, refund via BSP is not allowed unless we have authority from the airline or consolidator to submit RA. Failure to do so will result in ADM's.

Always answer email questions in the order that you receive them and maintain a respectful tone while stating facts. Example; Hi (first name), Unfortunately, it has not been possible to rebook your ticket. The airline's rules state that you must rebook your ticket at least XX days before departure, and the latest date for rebooking has now passed. This means that we are unfortunately unable to rebook your ticket. Kind regards, <@Agent first name + first letter of surname> <@Brand>

Rebooking request: apply the respective involuntary service fee per passenger during standard FM rebooking routines. ATTENTION: If the airline offers a flexibility in the fare rules, according to which the penalty is waived B no policy is visible in COVID-19/FMtrave alert related docs, you have to charge the standard voluntary rebooking fees per person! 4. Booking with at least one canceled segment in GDS itinerary (segment status UN) for which the airline has proposed a valid alternative (segment status TK) or the booking has a direct alternative segment (segment status TK) without cancellation status For specific guidelines of fees applicability for Schedule change cases, check here. Step 3 Parent step: 1 Involuntary fees SC/FM FAQ 1. The customer is unwilling to accept our involuntary service fee. What should I do? This is a service fee we charge to assist and process the customer's request. If needed, the agents can redirect the customer to our FAQ on-site where this is explained as well. For helpful phone scripts check here. It is not allowed to redirect the customer to our Customer Relations Department and encourage them to raise a claim there. If needed to escalate a case, this should be done to the respective Team Lead/ Supervisor. 2. Which fee should we charge in case of cancellation due to FM where the airline provides rebooking flexibility/open or voucher, but the cancellation has to be done by the fare rules?

If the order is FM affected, NO  fee applies, regardless of the YY policy for refund (full refund or refund by the fare rules). ATTENTION: By FM affected we mean a booking that falls under FM policy announced either via FM TA or COVID-19 docs in Edvin. Below scenarios are considered FM affected: There is at least one UN segment in the PNR and there is an FM policy allowing a full refund. There is an HK segment in the PNR and there is an FM policy allowing a full refund. There is a UN segment in the PNR, BUT the airline is NOT offering a full refund. Nevertheless, this information is stated in the policy under FM-related docs. 3. Do we update the templates manually in regards to the involuntary cancellation service fee? Answer: No, you do not need to update the wording of the template manually. You only need to insert the amount of the respective involuntary cancellation fee in the local currency of the customer. For the pricelist check here. ATTENTION: for exceptional handling markets/airlines, if the template includes the service fee field, you shall insert 0. 4. Are the involuntary service fees charged per order or per person? All involuntary service fees are charged per person. The only exceptional waiving routine may be applied for customers who have raised their requests prior to the fee restructuring and have complained about different fee value. For the related routine check here. 5. Are the involuntary service fees applicable for LCC bookings?

Yes, involuntary service fees are applicable for orders including LCC bookings. 6. Are the involuntary service fees applicable for B2B partners? Yes, involuntary service fees are applicable for B2B partners with the exception of B.com orders. 7. What should I do if the customer has a flexible ticket? Order falls under Force Majeure scenario: The customer can choose either to use the flexible ticket or to keep it for further changes. For detailed guidelines check here. Order falls under Schedule change scenario: Passenger is not able to use flexible ticket in case of schedule change. Follow the general guidelines here.

8. What should I do in case of Multi PNR if only the outbound PNR is FM affected and eligible for a full refund but for the inbound PNR  which has HK segments, no FM policy was announced and the cancellation has to be processed against fare rules. Which fee shall I charge for cancellation? If one of the PNRs is not FM affected then the standard voluntary cancellation fees will apply. ATTENTION: By not FM affected we mean a booking that has all flights confirmed (HK status) in the PNR and does NOT fall under any FM policy announced either via FM TA or COVID-19 docs in Edvin. 9. What should I do if one PNR is eligible for a full refund due to SC/FM and the other PNR is cxl /refund against fare rules only? Which fee shall I charge for cancellation? If the whole order is canceled due to FM and the 2nd PNR is FM affected, however, the airline does not offer a full refund then we need to cancel and apply only our involuntary cancellation service fee if applicable. ATTENTION: By FM affected we mean a booking that falls under FM policy announced either via FM TA or COVID-19 docs in Edvin. Below scenarios are considered FM affected: There is at least one UN segment in the PNR and there is an FM policy allowing a full refund. There is an HK segment in the PNR and there is an FM policy allowing a full refund. There is a UN segment in the PNR, BUT the airline is NOT offering a full refund. Nevertheless, this information is stated in the policy under FM-related docs. 10.

Do we charge the involuntary service fee for orders where the refundable amount is less than the value of the involuntary cancellation service fee? No, we don’t charge the involuntary service cancellation fee, but the customer's order becomes fully non refundable. Reminder: check the CXL service fee waived due to local legislation here. 11. The airline allows along with the FM rebooking, a free of charge NACO/NACH. What do we charge from our side in such cases? We charge our involuntary service fee if applicable and standard NACO/NACH handling fee. 12. What should I charge if the pax is calling us the same day as when they booked, flights are confirmed and both the FM policy for HK flights and the void + rebook process can be applied? You proceed with the void + rebook process along with the relevant voluntary rebooking service fees. Passengers should be aware of the travel restrictions for their nationality or any ongoing extraordinary circumstances before they book, which means that they intended to travel regardless. Therefore the rebookings cannot be considered FM affected if performed on the same day. Step 4 No linked steps INVOL fee waiver - cxl with YY (no ETG claim) - (Not in use) For cancellation requests in regard to orders affected by Force Majeure ,Schedule change and CXL Protection scenarios, if the customer has initiated the refund directly with the airline, we are not allowed to charge our service cancellation fee.

This policy applies for all markets and all sites. Please note for all markets and SC/FM refund requests, we don't charge any fee BUT if the customer initiated the refund with the airline directly, we use a different cancellation reason to skip the part of ETG involvement of claiming the tickets. Most common applicable scenarios: LCC bookings, where ETG can not handle the cancellation and therefore we always refer the customer to the airline directly 
LCC/GDS bookings, where the customer contacted the airline on their own initiative and the carrier has refunded the booking/ticket already without any ETG action

GDS booking, on case to case basis if for any reason ETG can not assist with the refund of the ticket (i.e.: the airline informs ETG that the customer has to reach out to them directly to initiate the refund) ATTENTION: The service fee waiver is applicable only if the ticket refund was initiated by the customer directly with the airline. If a customer has only canceled the segments with the carrier, but the ticket is not refunded, the case is not eligible for this waiver! For multi PNRs order, the service fee waiver applies ONLY if refunds for all PNRs have been initiated by the customer directly with the airline! How to identify if the ticket/booking is eligible for waiver? For LCC: Check OTRS/Edvin docs to identify if booking is affected by FM/SC For more details on FM/SC handling check standard routines here. ETG can not assist in canceling the booking or customer claims that the booking has already been canceled with the carrier For GDS: ATTENTION: Do NOT refer the customer to the airline for refund, unless otherwise stated in Edvin docs! Check PNR history/Edvin docs and standard routines to identify if the booking is affected by FM/SC Check the ticket record. Ticket should show status R/RFND or the ticket record will not be retrievable.

Partial Refund According to some fare rules, a partial refund is permitted, see example below. For this to apply, the information regarding this has to be noted in both fare rules.

WHEN COMBINING NON-REFUNDABLEFARES WITH REFUNDABLEFARES 
1.THEAMOUNTPAID ONEACHREFUNDABLEFARE COMPONENTISREFUNDED. 2.THEAMOUNTPAIDONEACHNON-REFUNDABLEFARE COMPONENTWILLNOTBEREFUNDED. 3.WHENCOMBININGFARESCHARGETHESUMOF THE CANCELLATION FEES OFALL CANCELLED FARE 
COMPONENTS. Be aware that sometimes the fare basis is stated per fare component, per direction or per segment. Then you need to reed all rules and then apply per fare, direction or segment. In cases of different fare rules you charge one fee, the highest, if that is mentioned in BOTH fare rules (see example below). WHEN MORE THAN ONE FARE COMPONENT IS CHANGED 
THE HIGHEST PENALTY OF ANY OF THE CHANGED FARE 
COMPONENTS WILL APPLY. Different fare rules, in both nothing is mentioned about which penalty to charge --> charge both penalties in case there are two or more fare components. More information can be found here. If it is stated in the rule that cancellation fee is 180 EUR, our fee will come to that, see pricelist in Edvin. Calculate the total cost in the passengers own currency. Airline penalty in percentage Sometimes fare rules says "CHARGE 50 PERCENT FOR CANCEL/REFUND." 
The cancellation/refund fee amount is then 50% of the base fare, if nothing regarding taxes is mentioned. Sometimes the fare rule says 50% of the fare plus YR/YQ taxes, then the cancellation/refund fee amount is then 50% of the base fare and the mentioned taxes.

For more information on how to calculate the penalty if it is mentioned in percentage, click here. How to calculate the price for a refund on different fare base stated partial refund on specific fare base Check Fare calculation BCN QR X/DOH QR CPT234.10MN X/JNB QR X/DOH QR BCN206.88NUC440.9? 8END ROE0.918404 Check NUC (GDS currency) for the destination where the farebase ends in this case CPT 234.10. (Sometimes a price can appear after Q that is an extra tax do not calculate on that) NUC times ROE to see the price in base fare currency. To calculate partial refund: 
Use FQD without issuing date to see price for a one way. Also check today's taxes. Basefare on that including taxes minus penalty fee.

Use FQP script for a one way price and today's (current) taxes if necessary according to rule. Cancellation fee waived for illness or death by the airline Some airlines allow waiving of their fees in case of illness or death of a passenger or their family member. Unless it is specified or the travel partner is a family member that can be proved, there is no guarantee that the airline will give any refund for the travel partner, even being in the same PNR. Please inform passengers that they need to send in a medical/death certificate in English or in the official language of the airline if this waiver is applicable! If we need to apply also for a refund for family members travelling together (if it's allowed by the carrier), then passengers must also submit a certificate of kinship in English or in the official language of the airline. Below is an example of how airlines mention in the fare rules of their tickets that a medical or death exception is possible. For the detailed routine follow the instructions HERE When sending to refund; use Modify Order in Edvin and choose "Airline fee". On "Other info to BO" write YY waiver acc to rule" Email routine: Customer cancels against medical certificate/death certificate through the airline fare rules. Cancellation by telephone Cancel the booking according to the customer's wishes and follow Modify Order in Edvin and choose "CAirline fee" (On Other info to BO write "YY waiver acc to rule").

Also, send a cancellation confirmation from Edvin. The agent can refer the customer directly to etraveli.com/medcert as we need to get the consent handle sensitive information and share the information with the airline. Keep in mind that the certificate needs to be in English for us to send it forward to the airline. The certificate ends up in category 160.7, which is handled by CR (CR will then change to category 120.12 which is handled by BO). Cancellation by e-mail Read fare rules and cancel the trip according to the customer's wishes and send cancellation confirmation to the customer from Edvin with template for waiver in rules. In email we will inform customer on how to send us the certificate via our website. The original email shall be permanently closed.

pdf_name: Guidelines for Providing Ticket Numbers to Airline Support to Avoid ADMs (Exceptional scenarios).pdf
paragraph:
Description There are scenarios when the new and/or old ticket numbers are requested to be provided to the airline, whenever authorization is needed as per Edvin Documents. Pay attention to the airline guidelines after receiving the authorization. Usually, they request exceptional flow to be followed during or after reissue, for reporting purposes. Such scenarios can be found below : 1) Waiver Authorization 
2) Name Correction 
3) Visa Rejection 
4) Medical/Death Certificate 
5) Irregularities (Other airlines involved). Actions that agents need to take FL and/or SC agents contact the airline and request a waiver as per guidelines in Edvin Documents. FL and/or SC agent should provide the airline ticket number and our request with a clear explanation. The airline’s representative provides the waiver and requests us to report back after reissuing new and/or old ticket number. FL and/or SC agents should request the below information from the airline representative: Waiver code/ Endorsement Deadline to provide the new and /or old ticket number/ extra information Way of reporting to the airline the required information (phone, email) Any other special flow ETG needs to follow as per the airline's request 
FL and/or SC agents need to check SSR lines for any important information added by an airline representative. FL and/or SC agent add clear notes via register errand.

FL/ SC agents should add detailed actions that SL needs to follow under Rebooking Wizard → Information to Ticketing. General rules for Naco/Nach !!IMPORTANT!! General guidelines but no guarantees \*Must double check Docs in Edvin\* No middle name is needed in the reservation (DOCS needs to be inserted according to passport though if traveling to the USA) 1-3 letters as long as it doesn't alter the pronunciation and the first letter of first/surname is correct At least one of surname and first name (within Europe) Always ask for any relevant documents (passport, ID, etc) if mentioned in Edvin docs., through Etrack and register the Etrack number in the register errand. When sending the Etrack Email to the customer make sure to follow the instructions here (select the market of the customer and “send & close” option) When is it a name change vs. name correction? This might differ from airline to airline, but we do follow some general rules:
·If changing to another personName Change NACH
· If the same person,but adding a middle name/last name/ Name Correction NACO changing the last name due to marriage and so on
Check in Edvin if it is permitted/necessary to change or correct the name. If it is multiple airline tickets or codeshare flights: Usually, it is not possible to make a name change or correction due to technical issues or due to the different booking systems. It is always a case-to-case policy, so the agents need to contact the airline unless otherwise mentioned Edvin Docs.

This means that if there is no information in Edvin Docs, the agents need to contact the airline (validating carrier) in order to be informed about the policy. Name on the ticket has to be exactly as on the passport/visa when traveling to China/Australia/New Zealand/Korea/Japan. If possible; cancel against the fare rule (our voluntary cancellation service fee will be charged). If less than 24 hours to departure, please check with your support team if it's possible to change or correct the name. pdf_name: How to calculate the penalty when it is mentioned as percentage of the fare in the ticket rules.pdf
paragraph:
Applicable fare rules as an example: According to  the fare rules, the penalty for the OB is  60% of the fare and for the IB is 80% of the fare. Both penalties apply per fare component and in case of combination of the fares both penalties apply.
FARE USD745.00 TOTAL GBP1126.89 EQUIVALENT FARE PAID GBP589.00 FARE CALCULATION
Step 1: Calculate the total penalty in NUC In the fare calculation on the ticket we see that the first fare component from LOS to LON costs 637.50 NUC and the second fare component from LON to LOS costs 107.50 NUC. Since both penalties will apply according to the fare rules stated above, the total penalty in NUC is: 60% \* 637.50 NUC + 80% \* 107.50 NUC = 382.5 NUC+ 86.00 NUC = 468.5 NUC Step 2: Convert it to the currency of the fare: In the fare calculation ROE (Rate Of Exchange) is to be found too. In this case it is equal to 1.00. So, the penalty in USD is: 468.5 NUC  \* ROE 1.00 = 468.5 USD Step 3: Convert the fare amount to the currency of the equivalent fare using the currency convertor in Edvin (Order date)

paragraph: FARE USD745.00 TOTAL GBP1126.89 EQUIVALENT FARE PAID GBP589.00 FARE CALCULATION

pdf_name: How to calculate the penalty when it is mentioned as percentage of the fare in the ticket rules.pdf
paragraph: Step 4: Inform the passenger: If the customer’s currency is the same as the equivalent’s fare one, then the 370.14 GBP is the penalty that needs to be communicated with the passenger. Otherwise, the agent needs to convert the penalty to the currency of the customer via Edvin currency converter again. Suggestion: In case there is only one penalty in percentage that applies for all sectors/ fare components/ pricing units : Mathematically the agents can speed up the process by calculating the penalty taking into consideration the total equivalent amount (avoiding the calculations in NUC). So, for a 60% penalty for the aforementioned ticket, where the equivalent fare is 589.00 GBP, the penalty is: 60% \* 589.00 GBP = 353.40 GBP After that the agents can go to step 4, skipping the previous ones.

Readingtime:2minutes Summary: conditions and procedures for Kayak US customers to cancel bookings within 24 hours for a full refund, including criteria, airline policies, and specific processes for voiding fees and verifying eligibility. Kayak US- 24h Cancellation and Void Procedure (booked via KAYAK only - now visible in Edvin) For Kayak US customers, we will waive our fees in case the airline provides a full refund in the case of a 24- hour cancellation and void. This is applicable under the following criteria (all must apply): 1. Cancellation completed within 24 hours from the time of payment. 2. Departure/destination or transit within the US. 3. The airline must offer a full refund as per Edvin's documents (no penalties). 4. The first departure date is at least 8 days ahead of the payment date. For example, if I book today, the 17th of December, the departure date should not be earlier than the 25th of December. If the departure date is the 25th of December, it can still be canceled for free; if it's the 24th of December, the 24-hour free cancellation does not apply. 5. Cancellation requests must come by phone or chat, as long as they are within 24 hours. Attention! For cases where the airline provides a 24-hour cancellation but with a penalty (e.g., 24-hour cancellation with TAP), we will charge our service fee and the airline's penalty as per the usual process. Please note we follow each airline's 24-hour cancellation policy.

In the case of a multi-PNR order, we need to verify if each PNR is eligible for the 24-hour Kayak US policy. For example, if a customer has a one-way ticket from MIA-LHR (1st PNR) and LHR-BER (2nd PNR), only the first PNR is eligible for the policy. The 2nd PNR can be canceled, but our fee will be applied (not applicable for B.com orders). For the 24-hour rule cancellation: Run Modify Order with the cancellation reason "24-hour airline rule." Make sure to write "Kayak US market 24-hour cancellation" in the errand. Follow the usual routine for 24-hour rule cancellation as described here. For Void cancellation: Run Modify order with the cancellation reason ‘’Void’’, the cancellation reason has been configured to waive automatically our fee for the eligible orders. We encourage you to provide your feedback about MOTO Payment feature via this form. Thank you! 1) What products can be added using Secure IVR payment? For all products and categories in add-on Cart, MOTO should be the preferred mode of payment unless: a) the Customer declines the option b)  if it is not technically possible for us to accept a MOTO payment (LATAM market and Maestro transaction for Australian/ Canadian markets) 2) If the Customer is not able to fulfill the payment on the IVR, can we still give them the Payment link option as per our standard routines? Yes, the payment link option should be offered as an ‘exception’, if the Customer declines or is unable to process the payment on the Secure IVR (example payment Links of situations could be: Customer does not have the credit card handy, a Credit card is expired). Please note, that whenever you offer a Payment link, you shall state in your errand the reason why you could not use MOTO (i.e: pax denied MOTO, MOTO not enabled etc.). 3) Can we use Secure IVR payment only for our ETG add-on products? Update: refer to question# 1. MOTO will be the preferred mode of payment for all products and charges (Airline and ETG) 4) Can we use Secure IVR payment if ETG add-on product is purchased together with Add on Sales/Our Service fee/ Airline cost and other Update: refer to question# 1.

MOTO will be the preferred mode of payment for all products and charges (Airline and ETG) 5) If the call drops involuntarily during the Secure IVR payment secure flow, do we need to contact the Customer? Yes, we will follow the standard routine for dropped calls which can be found here. 6) How can the staff identify whether Secure IVR payment can be used? When the Add-on cart is created, the MOTO Payment button gets activated on Edvin. Secure IVR  payment method will NOT be available for: LATAM markets, 
Orders from Gotogate.kr 
Customers from AU and CA markets, who wish to use a Maestro card. ATT: Please note that the MOTO payment method is still in its initial launching period. Currently, MOTO Payment method is available for specific languages markets (for details refer to initial blogpost here). For orders where MOTO Payment is not available yet, the respective MOTO Payment button is automatically deactivated in Edvin's Add on cart. 7) After entering the card details, will the IVR reconfirm the amount that the Customer will be paying?

No. It is therefore mandatory for staff to verbally inform Customers about the amount and the breakdown of the total cost (product & fees) that will be charged to the Customer’s card before transferring the call to the IVR. ALSO, Customers need to be made aware of the full details of the added service/product (those details need to be added by the agents in 'Text to Customer' field in the Add on Cart. Also, ensure the flight details are always verified before transferring the Customer to the IVR 8) What are the time frame restrictions to insert the card details on the IVR? \* Note:Thisinformationisonlyfortheagent'sawarenes andwi not becom unicatedtotheCustomer\* 30 seconds for Credit Card Number, 10 seconds for expiry date, and 10 seconds for CVV/CVC number. 9) How many attempts does the Customer get on the IVR in one go? Wrong details can be entered on the IVR a maximum of 3 times for each category (card number, expiration date, CVV). After which the Customer will be automatically redirected back to the agent. 10) What option must we select in Genesys in order to redirect the call to the IVR? [Red Button] “Send customer to secure Payment IVR”. ATT: Before sending the customer to IVR flow, you must always ensure first that the MOTO Payment button i available in your Add on cart in Edvin. 11) How will the agent identify if the call is connected to the IVR? A banner will appear on the top of the GENESYS window stating “Secure flow in progress”.

12) How will the agent get the notification on Genesys once the IVR flow is finalized? [Green Button] “Get token from Secure Payment IVR”. 13) If the card details are incorrectly entered by the Customer, will the agent receive the token on Genesys? No token would be generated in this case and you must ask the Customer to try again. Remember you must transfer the Customer to the IVR one more time. 14) If the card details were not inserted correctly by the Customer, what errors will the staff get on Genesys? - Invalid card details (incorrectly inserted card number) - Invalid expiration date (incorrectly inserted expiration date) - Invalid CVV(incorrectly inserted CVV) 16) Will there be only numbers in the payment token? No, it will be a combination of letters and numbers.

17) If a valid token has been pasted in Edvin, what icon will you see confirming that the token is correct? Green Tick. 18) What message will you see in Edvin if the payment was successful? “Payment was successfully executed”. 19) Where can we find in Edvin, if the payment is successfully fulfilled? 1) Under Add a Purchase, it will be marked with (MOTO) in the Payment Type colum 2) In the Payment transaction tab 20) Where can we find the services added with payments performed via Secure IVR in Edvin? Under AddOn Sales in Order Summary 21) What is the list of possible errors (Payment failed and the Customer was not charged), which we may receive after entering the token and clicking on the pay button in Edvin?

22) Can we send an email to the Customer, if the payment is unsuccessful and the Customer is asking for a written confirmation that the payment did not go through? Yes, we can send an email from Edvin using the email template “Secure IVR Payment attempt failed” (Under F - Others folder). This needs to be sent only if the Customer is asking for it. 23) What needs to be done in case of an unsuccessful payment? Offer to retry try the payment again via Secure IVR, preferably by using a different card. If the Customer declines the Secure IVR payment, you may offer the Payment link option as per the standard routines 24) What to do in case of fare increase or the cost of the service/ancillary has changed Check the cost difference, if the Customer agrees to cover the additional charge Follow the Secure IVR payment flow to collect the cost 
Do not suggest the payment link option in such cases, as it increases the risk of losing the availability again 25) What if the Customer declines to cover the additional charge and demands a refund of the initial payment? Follow the standard routine for a refund of service using Modify order. 26) What if we are unable to confirm the change request due to technical issues? Follow the standard routine for a refund of service using Modify order. 27) In an event where the request cannot be finalized due to name correction or any request for which we need to contact the Airline/SupPayment Link what must be done?

Collect the amount using Secure IVR payment and manually assign the file to the Support Queue from Edvin 28) In which markets will Secure IVR not be available? LATAM markets 29) What type of card payments are accepted on the IVR? All card types are accepted on our site. The only exception is Maestro cards for The Canadian and Australian markets. Agents must advise Customers from these markets that Maestro is not accepted and they should use any other card they may have before processing further steps. 30) What if it’s a CC2C Booking, can we use Secure IVR payment to collect the refund fee? Yes 31) When the call gets routed to the IVR will the staff on the other end be able to hear the Customer response or not? No, Agent will not be a part of the IVR Flow.

32) How can I check if Secure IVR is activated for the market I am servicing? You will see the MOTO payment button in the Add on Cart in Edvin. Besides this, the launch dates by market will be shared as an Announcement on Shelf as and when available. ATT: The fact that you are technically able to send the customer to IVR flow in Genesys, does not mean that MOTO Payment is enabled as a payment method for this specific order! Always check Edvin! 33) For how long is the token visible on Genesys, in case the agent needs to copy it again? For as long as the call is open with the agent. It will close the script after the agent enters the wrap-up code and click on done 34) If an agent needs to send the Customer back to the IVR for collecting additional charges, will the page on Genesys get refreshed with a new token code after the transaction? Yes, a new unique token code will be generated for the second transaction. 35) If the Customer has already had 2 unsuccessful attempts on the IVR and wishes to try with a different card, can we connect the call to the IVR again? Agents should manually send the customer to the Secure IVR not more than twice (first attempt included). If the Customer gets a decline on the first attempt, always check if they can try with another card before transferring the second time. After a second unsuccessful attempt, always offer the payment link option. 36) What languages will the IVR messaging be available in?

IVR will go live for each market in their specific language. Go-live dates will be shared. 37) Can an agent update the amount in the Add-on cart after the token number is generated? Yes, as long as the token is unused. The token number is an authorization by the Customer for us to use the card for the payment however it is not linked to any specific amount. If the Agent updates the Add-on cart with a new amount, he must ensure the new charges (along with break-up) and travel details are reconfirmed with the Customer before proceeding with using the token on Edvin. 38) If the call gets disconnected after flight details and charges are confirmed with the Customer but before the token is generated, should the outbound call be made through the respective queue to be able to offer MOTO? As per current routine, the agent is obliged to call back the passenger anytime when the call drops. In order for the IVR flow option to be available, the agent will have to create a new outgoing interaction on behalf of queue. Otherwise IVR flow will not be accessible. Callback process has been updated with this information in relevant Shelf page. 39) What details are visible on the payment confirmation receipt - will this have both the flight details and amount (\*\*critical to have both to handle disputes from Customers\*\*)

The payment confirmation receipt will have exactly the same form as it has now with PL. The amounts are visible as per Products added in the Add on cart, although the flight/ancillary details will be visible as per 'Text to Customer' field in Add on cart. A reminder - Agents must always ensure the right service 'details' are added in the Add-on cart and are also verbally confirmed to the Customer before MOTO is processed. 40) Since payment will be completed by the FL/SC agents would it be their responsibility to remove this from the Edvin Payment dash? The MOTO Payment will not appear on the Payment Dashboard for further handling as PL does. Agent mus only check for successful payment confirmation in Edvin and be responsible for follow-up actions. 40)  Can MOTO be offered as a payment option for Chat? The MOTO payments option will not be available for the Chat channel for now and agents must process a payment link 41)  Can you void payment if incorrectly processed through MOTO This is not currently possible. 42)  Is it possible to transfer calls to MOTO IVR of a different language if the Customer requests? This is not possible currently. 43) Shall MOTO Payment be used also when handling Schedule Change requests? Yes, it is a preferred method whenever the request can be handled or followed up by the phone agent. For details please check relevant shelf guidelines under Paymentmethodsforpost-saleservices.

44) Do we need to queue the file to the Support team manually, after collecting the amount using MOTO Payment for name correction/name change, or where an Airline contact is required? Yes, we need to queue the file to the Support queue manually for them to handle the file 45) Can we use MOTO payment for a schedule change file where the passenger is asking for a second alternative and authorization is not required? Yes, we will use MOTO payment. 46) For a schedule change case where we need authorization from the airline by email, can we use MOTO payment? Yes, we will use MOTO payment and will queue the file to the respective queue manually for them to obtain authorization from the airline 47) If the passenger is asking for an alternate flight option due to schedule change and authorization is needed by phone from the Airline. In such cases can we use MOTO payment? No, we will send a payment link to the Customer as per the normal routine.

48) What to do if the ‘Send customer to secure Payment IVR’ button is not visible in Genesys? Make sure that the panel of your on-going interaction is not hidden. Click on buttons shown on the below image: Remember that for outbound calls you always have to perform the interaction on behalf of a queue. If the above points are met and you still face an issue with unavailable IVR flow, kindly use the feedback form to report the error received. 49) Can I forward the customer to IVR flow for any order where I see ‘Send customer to secure Payment IVR’ in Genesys interaction? NO! ‘Send customer to secure Payment IVR’ button is enabled for all queues in Genesys, but it doesn’t mean that MOTO is an available form of payment for all orders. Always check the Add on cart in Edvin to see if the MOTO Payment button is enabled. Otherwise you risk sending the customer to IVR flow for an order where you won’t be able to charge him/her via MOTO! 50) Can I use MOTO Payment feature when my call is under active monitoring? No, MOTO Payment feature is not technically available when the call is under active monitoring (Supervisor's monitoring or other agent's shadowing). In such cases, follow PL routine.

51) Can I offer MOTO payment on Booking.com order? Yes, provided that MOTO is available on this particular market. MOTO payment is now enabled on Booking.com orders for the enabled markets. Remember that for orders where MOTO Payment is not available yet, the respective MOTO Payment button is automatically deactivated in Edvin's Add on cart.

On a go forward, when we receive a name correction or name change request from anyone who has booked through the following 4 sites, we MUST initiate the name correction/change with the airline. A change to a different passenger is not permitted except if the airline's policy allows it. Gotogate BR Mytrip BR Flightnetwork BR Booking.com BR As per Brazil’s legislation (ANAC, art. 8) they have mandated the requirement of reaching out to the airline in writing whenever a  name correction or change is being requested. Important points to keep in mind… Whether or not the airline is able to do the name correction or name change, we must inquire with the airline in writing so we have it on record that we initiated the request 
Our naco/nach fee will always apply, regardless if the airline cost is FOC 
You should charge our service fees only if the name correction/change has been approved by the airline, along with airline cost for the correction. No fees shall be prepaid before we are sure that the name correction/change is possible. 
Majority of the name correction/change will be for Gol Linhas Aéreas G3, Latam LA, Azul Airlines AD & LATAM Airlines Brasil JJ. For LCC bookings, where in Edvin documents it is stated that we should NEVER contact the airline, please refer the customers to the airline directly. 
For all other booking sources including Consolid, we must assist with the naco/nach, follow the normal routines

paragraph: How to handle Infant Naco/Nach requests when booking under the void window Description: In case the customer contacts us for NACO/NACH about INF (infant) passenger while void is still possible. We will propose to issue a new ticket for Infant and Adult tickets who are associated with Infant, while we are voiding the old tickets with the wrong name. Step by step for void & new ticket: 1. Check if a void is possible and if it is in a void window. If the booking is out of the Void window or not possible to void, follow the NACO general process mentioned in Shelf and Edvin Docs. 2. If Void is possible; Check the availability for the same flights before advising the Void option. 3. Inform the customer of the applicable fare difference for both passenger Infant and Adult tickets who are associated with Infant (Our fees for both Adult and infant will not be charged). The new ticket fare difference should be calculated with the original ticket fare and taxes. Collect the payment via Moto during the call or via the Payment link. Also, collect the passport copy or identity card copy from the passenger via etrack. Attn: Inform the customer that providing the correct spelling on the call is their responsibility. Otherwise, the customer must submit the relevant document. 4. Once we receive the payment from the customer, Split the Adult on whom the Infant is associated if needed (If there is more than one Adult) and link the PNR in Edvin. 5.

RefundApplication Search Search for Refund Applications by RA Number,PNR,Ticket Number or Order Number Allowed characters are A-Z 9-U and dash (-) Search Once the RA is found you will be able to see the status, the amounts, the dates of application and response, and in case the RA is rejected also the reason for rejection. If the RA is not found through the tool, please escalate the request to the FL Coordinator in duty. Search RefundApplications RA statuses you may come upon: Authorized: The RA raised has been checked by the airline and they have authorized the refund to us. The fact that the status is ‘Authorized’ does not necessarily mean that the amount is paid back to us already. Usually the refund to us needs approximately 8 weeks to be credited back to us, but there are still exception airlines that might take longer so please do not take the timeframe as a guaranteed rule.

If the RA is authorized close to the date that you are checking the status, no action needs to be taken. Please advise the custom to wait. If the RA status has been authorized for more than 8 weeks and the passenger has not received any refund yet, you may escalate the order to Manager, Team Leader or FL Coordinator to advise you for further action.

Billed:  The RA raised has been authorized and the amount is refunded to us already. If the RA is ‘Billed’ close to the date that you are checking the status, no action needs to be taken. Please advise the custom to wait. If the RA status has been ‘Billed’ for more than 8 weeks and the passenger has not received any refund yet, you may escalate the order to Manager, Team Leader or FL Coordinator to advise you for further action. Rejected: The RA raised has been checked by the airline and they have rejected the reason for refund. Almost at all times, there is justification of the reason they have not accepted it. You may escalate the order to your Manager, Team Leader or FL Coordinator so that they can escalate this to SL. Pending: The RA is not yet checked from the airline, advise the customer to wait. No need for further escalation. Sent to Airline: Same as pending, the RA is not yet checked from the airline, advise the customer to wait. No need for further escalation. Under investigation:The RA claimed is currently checked by the airline, advise the customer to wait. No need for further escalation. Changed by agent: The RA claimed is currently checked by the airline, advise the customer to wait. No need for further escalation. After collecting the required information, please inform the customer accordingly for the status of his request and proceed with any further actions. Escalation required: If we receive a great complaint, which is justified (ex.

extreme delay), you may escalate the order to your Manager, Team Leader or FL Coordinator so that they can escalate this to SL. Please remember that critical thinking is required for such kinds of escalations.

Terminology
Please ALWAYS ensure you review the airline policy outlined in Edvin Documents to con rm there are no exceptions, as
illustrated in the examples below. Involuntary Reissue / Revalidation
Accept the alternative means whenever a schedule change is done on the reservation the ticket numbers
remain the same, and no need to get the tickets reissued/revalidated as per carrier policy in Edvin
Documents, even if the time is not matching as long as the date, ight number and airports are the same. Customer can just present his original ticket at the airport for check in, even though his new itinerary is
di erent with the ticket. Note that in this scenario the con rmation of the segments (ERK/EWR) is required. Revalidation -  It's a process in which whenever a change is done on the reservation the ticket numbers
remain the same. The information on the itinerary needs to match with the ticket. Reissue means replacement of an existing air ticket with a new air ticket. Involuntary reissue allows you to
reissue a ticket without an extra cost or waiving a fee, when there is an involuntary rerouting due to
unplanned disruptions or planned schedule changes by the airline. Obviously reissuing a ticket is more time consuming and costly than revalidation, but not all date changes
require reissue.

pdf_name: Content - 01. General Info for Flight Irregularities 20250310-071732.pdf
paragraph:
Re-Routing means a change in the origin, destination, transit, or stopovers originally ticketed. Involuntary refund
Involuntary Refunds means a refund of an unused ticket or portion there of or an unused miscellaneous
charges order required as a result of the carrier cancelling a ight, failing to operate a ight according to
schedule, failing to stop at a point to which the passenger is destined or is ticketed to stop over, or
causing the passenger to miss a connecting ight, being unable to provide previously con rmed space,
substituting a di erent type of equipment or class of service or where, because of safety or legal
requirements or the condition or conduct of the passenger, carriage is refused. An electronic ticket can be refunded either directly via the GDS in the o ce the ticket was issued or
through BSPlink. [GDS] Global Distribution System, such as Amadeus, Sabre, or Galileo. [BSP] Billing and Settlement Plan is an IATA electronic billing system to run and simplify the interchange of
data and funds between travel agencies and airlines. Sounds complicated, but in plain English, BSP is a
payment mediator between airlines and travel agents. EMD
An EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) is an electronic voucher issued by an airline or designated
agency. The EMD is of the value indicated on the front, and is issued as a coupon to be used for the
purpose described thereon, or for handling fees.

pdf_name: Content - 01. General Info for Flight Irregularities 20250310-071732.pdf
paragraph:
Usually the EMD issued for ancillaries via GDS systems, such as baggage, seats, etc. As EMD corresponds to a ticket customer can nd it in the booking reference on his/her ticket or in the
con rmation e-mail we have sent to them after completing their reservation. Waiver: What is this? Travel waivers sometimes refer to situations in which an airline allows a passenger to waive travel
because there are safety concerns. For example, a waiver allows customers to change their itinerary with
no fare di erences if they remain in the same cabin as originally booked, such kind of criteria can be
found under Edvin Documents. Note that airline use di erent waivers for their policy or ows. For example airline can request to add an
endorsment during cancellation or reissue, or add an OSI line before any actions, or add a Tour Code in a
speci c eld. It is important to mention that di erent processes should be followed for each waiver, so FL agent need to
provide clear instruction to SL agent of the action he/she needs to follow. Inactive segments and non show
Please keep in mind that there are some airline companies that require us to remove the inactive
segments from the PNR, before the departure. The inactive segments usually have a status UN/UC/US/NO or HX. The Ticketing team is working on removing the inactive segments to avoid any ﬁnancial costs for the
company. What this means is that sometimes you might ﬁnd PNRs without ﬂight segments, speciﬁcally for orders
with close departures.

pdf_name: Content - 01. General Info for Flight Irregularities 20250310-071732.pdf
paragraph:
You will probably see the following in GDS as an indication of the above (but sometimes it will be a regular
ghostline):
MIS 1A HK1 STO 04MAR-SEGMENT REMOVED TO AVOID CHARGES
All PNRs impacted by Covid19 with inactive segments (UN/HX/NO/UC) we will now handle as per the
airline's FM guidelines in Travel Alert pages. One such segment in the order (not referring to Multiple
PNRs) is enough to consider it aﬀected and handle as per FM policy. This applies to all types of cases, refund/open ticket/voucher/rebookings. Handle the PNR accordingly, regardless of the original departure date. Furthermore, when we follow FM policy, if the airline has a deadline to fulﬁll a certain process (deadlines
for rebookings etc.), this cannot be ignored even if we have a case with inactive segments. We have to
stick to the process and follow the airline's guidelines. Please note that if the segments were active (HK) before the customer being marked as a no-show, we
have to follow normally the no-show policy. Thus, you need to check the history of the PNR in GDS to be
sure of how to proceed in each case. A ‘no show’ designation refers to a ticketed passenger that has failed to check in or board their booked
 ight. Some airlines used the de nition "NoShow" even before departure which might restrict some
actions like rebookings and cancellations.

Schedule change within 24 hours handling
1. What is a 24 hour schedule change? A 24 hour schedule change refers to any changes to a ight’s schedule that occurs within 24 hours of the
originally planned departure time. Airlines usually have speci c policies and procedures for handling these
last minute schedule changes, which may include o ering rebooking options, refunds, or other
accommodations depending on the severity of the change. According to the contracts with carriers, airlines handle all the schedule changes that occur within 24 hours
of the original departure date. 2.

How do you identify a 24 hour schedule change? To identify a 24 hour schedule change, log into the relevant system and check the PNR history. Often,
schedule changes close to departure may not be re ected in the PNR. If the change is not visible in the PNR,
use the DO command in Amadeus (e.g., DOLH170/02JUL):
DO: Always stable. LH170: Operating airline and ight number. /: Always stable. 02JUL: Date of the scheduled ight. In the case that the DO command does not work, check the ight status from the airline site and redirect the
customer to the airline if no schedule change information is found even on the airline website ight status
and DO command. DO command can be used for future ights as well as for ights
up to three days in the past. After verifying the schedule change
with the DO command, please contact the airline to get
authorization for any involuntary changes. The DO command is
only for checking ight status, and it cannot be used to process
involuntary changes. 3. How do you calculate the 24 hour schedule change? To compare the time between the rst city where the SC occurred and Zulu time, use the Amadeus system. Whenever a SC is made to the PNR by the carrier, the event time will appear in the PNR history in Zulu (GMT)
time. Therefore, you need to calculate the Zulu time in relation to the departure city's local time to accurately
identify the event timing. Example: 
Departure from BOM is at 1900 on July 3.

Eg : AI123 Y 03JUL BOMLHR HK1 1900 0700+1
Now the schedule change (SC) occurred at 10 PM Zulu time on July 2. So now to calculate the if the schedule change was within 24 hours use below entry :
Amadeus Entry : DDGMT2200/BOM/02JUL24
DD : Command 
GMT : Zulu Time 
2200 : SC occurred time in Amadeus 
BOM : Departure city 
02JUL24 : Event date 
The result :  BOM TIME IS 1130/1130A ON WED03JUL24        
The result shown above (11:30 AM, 03 July) is the date and time when the schedule change occurred. By
comparing this with the ight’s departure time, we can determine if the schedule change was within 24
hours. In the example given, the schedule change occurred within 24 hours of the ight's departure. 4. How do we handle 24 hour schedule changes in the script? We currently have a setting in the GDS SC script that automatically removes cases from the queue when a
schedule change occurs within 24 hours of the original departure. If the automation fails, the case will fall
into the manual queue. 5. How to handle 24 hour schedule changes within 24 hours in the
manual queue? When an SC agent receives a case:
If the customer contacts you:
First, identify if the schedule change occurred within 24 hours of departure. If the change is not re ected in the PNR history, use the DO command in Amadeus. If the DO command does not work, use the airline ight status referring airline sites.

Once the schedule change is identi ed, inform the customer about the schedule change and if the
customer is asking for a change, assist the customer if you are able to handle the schedule change. If you are not able to handle the schedule change, then redirect the customer. It is the airline's
responsibility to handle the schedule change that occurs within 24 hours of departure. Register the errand. Click here for more information. Remove the case from all the SC queue
6. How to handle schedule changes that occur more than 24
hours. In cases where SC occurs more than 24 hours before departure and is not re ected in GDS, agents will still
follow the above guideline, but not refer the customer to the airline. Instead, they will escalate to the support
queue for further action after using the DO command or checking the ight status to obtain the airline
authorization/waiver code. Above guidelines are only for NON VI cases, as for VI we handle
all schedule changes regardless of departure date. Click here for SC VI guidelines.

ARN FAQ
1. What is ARN? ARN stands for Acquirer Reference Number. It is the reference number given to a refund transaction when it is processed. This number can 
be used by the Customer/Bank to locate the refund processed at our end. 2. Why do we provide ARN to a Customer? When a payout has been processed on our end, but the Customer has trouble locating the refund in their accounts, we provide them with 
the ARN in order to contact their bank and locate the funds using the transaction reference. 3. What is PSP? PSP stands for Payment System Provider. They are online payment gateways that handle payment transactions on behalf of other 
companies. Basically they are our partners, handling our payments with Customers (in & out). However, in certain cases the PSP could be a direct provider with whom the Customer has a direct contract (eg: Klarna)
4. What are the main Payment Systems (PSP) we currently use? Checkout

cases we are not able to provide ARN.

The table below gives you a snapshot of which Payment systems have an ARN visible. For the detailed steps please follow the links for

 ow is a blind spot for us.

The shortcut stands for Electronic Miscellaneous Document.

When we add extra products like seating, baggage etc., for which the airline demands extra charge, we 
need to book the requested service, set a price and issue an EMD for this extra service.

ATT: Please note that the EMD for future travel due to corona (EMD voucher) is a diﬀerent procedure, 
please check the respective routine here.

an EMD for the whole connection in such PNR, the airlines involved in the itinerary need to

agreement and EMD will not be able to be issued on such a connection.

3. EMD can NOT be issued for part of outbound or part of inbound, only for whole outbound, whole 
inbound or whole ticket.

Customer Relations (CR) evaluates all medical certi cates and approves/denies refunds when a customer
cancels against cancellation protection.

When a customer wishes to cancel against cancellation protection
Make sure the booking includes cancellation protection.
If the departure date is far ahead, inform the customer we may require a further certi cate closer to
departure. 
Cancellation has to be done no later than 2 hours before the outbound ight. 
We will not evaluate certi cates where the customer is a no-show. 
Cancellation protection is not valid for a partially used ticket or for multi PNR when the outbound
 ight has been used. 
In case the customer has changed his ticket directly with the airline and claims a full refund at the
same time, the service is not provided. We do not o er a full refund while the tickets are active.
Always check the ticket status.
Cancel the PNR for the person who cannot travel.
From 10 May 2023, the administrative fee will NO longer be applied. For orders canceled before May 
10, the administrative fee of 15 euros is charged except for the customers who had purchased the 
Platinum Support Package. 
Run Modify order with ''Cancellation protection ETG'' reason. Send an email con rmation of the
cancellation from Edvin using the template for cancellation protection.
Αdvise the customer to upload the medical documents through this link https://www.
etraveligroup.com/medcert/ . The form is associated with the etrack category where all the
medical docs end up there. 
The email address medical.certi cate@support.etraveli.com is no longer valid!

If you, for some reason, need to send the con rmation via Etrack- use the correct standard reply (Canx
against med) and use the category "160.7 Medical Certi cate" that will direct the reply to Customer
Relations directly.
If you receive a medical certi cate in any other category you just need to recategorize it to 160.7 for
further assistance. Do not answer or close, just recategorize.
Due to GDPR not everyone has access to Etrack category 160.7 and can't see if we have received the
certi cate or not.
All certi cates that are sent to us by post will be scanned and visible for Customer Relations in a
certain inbox in Etrack (and of course, searchable for all other users)

Cancellation by email through incorrect category
If the customer requests to cancel and has attached a medical certi cate, the agent shall complete
the cancellation. Send an email con rmation of the cancellation from Edvin using the template for
cancellation protection, change to email to category 160.7 and reply with signature GDPR info, and
permanently close the email. The customer is asked to submit the certi cate via the correct form and
also leave his consent.
If the customer has not attached any medical certi cate, the agent sends an email con rmation of the
cancellation from Edvin using the template for cancellation protection. The original email can be
closed.
If there are any ambiguities about the cancellation, the agent changes the category (160.7) and the CR
team will reply to the email.

General rules
There is no urgent handling for medical certi cates so avoid such requests in regards to a refund.
If the customer is actually ill and cannot travel an urgent refund is not an issue as the person is in
fact ill no matter the refund or not.
No evaluation will be initiated if the booking is not canceled.
Never approve a certi cate by phone or email with the customer directly, it is not the responsibility of
any First line agent to do this.
Neither is it the responsibility of the agent to make sure the customer knows the Terms and
conditions of the cancellation insurance before cancelling, this is the sole responsibility of each
customer to check.
We can always recommend the customer to go through these again though, before con rming the
cancellation. For example, if a customer cancels due to pregnancy, this will be denied as the
cancellation insurance does not cover such conditions.
In case of change, either voluntary or involuntary, the product is not transferable even if only the hour
is changed.

The Cancellation Protection is valid for the following people in relation to one of
the travelers:
"Close relative" in this context means the insured party's husband, wife, children, grandchildren,
siblings, parents, grandparents or parents-in-law, or a person that the insured party lives with as a
couple as if they were married.
The cancellation protection is valid for everyone in the order. For example, if friends are traveling and
a parent of one of the travelers becomes ill and the certi cate is approved by CR, this covers all
people in the booking.
The cancellation protection covers immediate illness or death only. If the customer has become ill
after date of travel, this will not be approved. The illness has to prevent the traveler from traveling.
Hence, if the traveler is visiting someone who has become ill and therefore does not want to go, this
will not be approved as the traveler him/herself is not prevented from traveling (“purpose of travel no
longer existing” as per the below-stated condition).
If you feel that there are uncertainties when canceling, for example, the customer seems dishonest
(states he or she is NOT ill but will still send a medical certi cate either way), inform the customer
that we consider insurance fraud to be a very serious take.
Add any information in the booking for the evaluating department to see. Other dishonest situations
may be that the customer is not able to obtain a visa for travel, booked incorrect dates, etc.

What the cancellation protection does not cover
Remuneration which may be received from elsewhere, such as other cancellation protection or
insurance.
Phobia or anxiety in direct relation to ying.
Illness, accident, or injury of which you were aware (with which you were diagnosed) when concluding
the cancellation protection.
Chronic illnesses/infections/mental disorders, unless the person has been completely free of
symptoms/problems over the past six months, from the time of booking the trip. If the cancellation
relates to these symptoms, the diagnosis must be con rmed by a specialist.
Illness, accident or other repercussions due to pregnancy or childbirth.
Complications caused by alcohol, other intoxicants, sedatives or narcotics.
Costs arising due to the fact that the insured party delayed his/her cancellation of the travel
arrangement.
The purpose of the trip no longer existing.
Complications resulting from personally selected procedures and treatments, such as beauty
operations.
Any supplementary arrangements for the trip which are not included in the con rmation, such as
theatre tickets and suchlike.

Queue Item distribution
Introduction
This page gives an overview of how the queue item distribution system works in order to automatically assign
items from manual and custom queues to agents based on when we need to start the handling of an item,
and what tasks the agent should work on. Handle by
Handle by is the time when we need to have started the handling of an item. There are two types of handle
by, namely hard handle by and soft handle by.

Hard handle by is the time when we really need to
have started the handling of an item in order to complete it before it is too late. This could for example be 48
hours before next departure. Soft handle by is when we would like to have handled the item. This could for
example be 2 days after customer contacted us if the item is on a queue because of a customer interaction. Hard Handle by: We really need to have started the handling of an item by this time. In some cases it
might even be ok to call pax in the middle of the night in order to solve an issue if we have past this date. Soft Handle by: Mostly used to follow SLA:s by specifying when we would like to have started the handling
of an item. The soft handle by can never be past dated, and the hard handle by can never be before the soft handle by. In short: Queue Place time ≤ Soft handle by  ≤ Hard handle by
A brief overview of how a queue item distribution con guration could look like. O set groups
The o set groups de nes how to calculate the handle by for a given item. Both "hard" and "soft handle by" is
calculated by o setting a number of minutes from a Base Date. A negative number of minutes will give a time
before the base date, and a positive number will give a time after the base date. What base date you can
o set from depends on the entity that is on the queue. It can for example be "Queue place date" or "Next
segment departure".

There can be multiple o sets con gured, and the o set that gives the earliest time is
the one that will be used. O set groups
Example:
Assume that we have put the following order on the queue:
Order ABC:
Placed on queue: 2023-02-12 10:30
Next departure: 2023-02-23 14:15
And that the queue have the following con g:
Hard handle by con g:
"Next departure" with o set -1440 (24H before departure)
Soft handle by con g:
"Next departure" with o set -7200 (5 days before departure)
"Queue place date" with o set 4320 (3 days after put on queue)
Then we would get the following handle by:
Hard handle by: 2023-02-22 14:15 (24H before next departure)
Soft handle by: 2023-02-15 10:30 (3 days after put on queue, since that gave the earliest handle by out of
the two soft handle by con gs)
Handle by con g groups
The handle by con g groups de nes which o set groups that should be used to calculate handle by for a
given item. One item may match multiple con gs, and therefor multiple o set groups. Edvin will select the
earliest handle bys calculated by the o set groups that the con gs selected. What parameters that it is
possible to use to match against an item on the queue depends on what entity it is. If it is an Order, then it is
one set of parameters, and if it is an Errand case then it is another set of parameters.

Handle by con g groups in Edvin
Example:
Assume that we have put the following order on the queue:
Order XYZ:
Partner: Booking.com
Placed on queue: 2023-02-12 10:30
And that we have the following handle by con gs de ned for the queue:
Default con g (matches anything that is put on the queue)
Hard handle by: 
"Queue place date" with o set 30 days after put on queue
Soft handle by:
"Queue place date" with o set 10 days after put on queue
Partner con g (matches all orders with a partner that we want to give extra good service to):
Hard handle by:
"Queue place date" with o set 20 days after put on queue
Soft handle by:
"Queue place date" with o set 5 days after put on queue
Then we would get the following handle by since it was an partner order, and therefor matched the partner
con g:
Hard handle by: 2023-03-04 10:30
Soft handle by: 2023-02-17 10:30
Queue item distribution con g
In the queue item distribution con g we specify what con g should be used to calculate the handle by for a
queue. Here it is also possible to con gure what snooze labels and other settings on how the distribution
should work for a queue. Queue item distribution con g in Edvin
Work groups
Work groups is a way to de ne from which queues a set of agents should get assigned items from. A work
group can be scheduled to only be active during certain days and hours.

This can be used to only assign
items to agents under certain hours of the day when pax is most likely to be awake and able to answer a call
for instance. Over view of how an item is assigned to an agent based on what work groups the agent is part of. Work groups in Edvin
Members
A member of a work group is an agent that will be served items from this work group. One agent can be
member of several work groups and will then be served the most urgent item to be handled according to the
handle by strategies con gured. Work stream
What to work on in a work group is de ned by its work streams. A work stream is a queue and a queue view
that lters out the items to be handled by this work group. What properties it is possible to lter on in a
queue view depends on what entity type it is on the queue. Handle by strategies
We both want to make sure that we handle items on queue before it is too late and within a reasonable time
if it is a customer interaction that caused the item to be on the queue. To decide in what order items should
be picked from the queue the handle by strategies con g speci es a threshold for how far into the future we
should order the items according to their hard handle by, before switching to order them by soft handle by. We want to avoid having unhandled items with a hard handle by on times when no agent is working. The risk
for this can be minimised by increasing the hard handle by threshold the days before the weekend/vacation
period.

Some customers might make duplicate bookings due to an error message on our website or payment not
going through.

If the duplicate is with another website or airline, then the customer needs to provide us with the PNR so we
can double-check the duplicate, but we can only “handle” our own order and take the necessary actions on it. What parameters should we look at while checking if the duplicate is due to technical, payment, and/or
website problems? Listen to the customer rst and take notes on what they said happened. Did they receive an error
message, and what did it say? At which step of the booking process did it occur? Always check the time between the two duplicates – is it a relevant time? Was the duplicate made shortly
after? Always check when the con rmation was sent; was it delayed from our side?

Also, some other parameters that can give you a hint that a problem could have occurred during the payment
process:
Always check the payment information on the rst booking; can we see any disturbance in the payment? For example, we can see here that it took around 30 minutes to complete the payment. That is an indication
that something might have happened. Also, check if we have an error log in the order. For example, the error Message “Ett generellt fel har
uppstått” means that a general error has occurred. This log shows if the client got an error message. Important! This is still one parameter to look into, there are examples where customer gets an error message,
and we do not have this Error log in Edvin:
Very important! When the customer calls with a dupe booking same day or within 24h where applicable,
 always get the customer to con rm a cancellation of at least one of the orders. If we wait for escalation, then we lose the possibility to void or claim the 24-hour rule, which results in

General information & Flow concept
Brazilian law has a very strict legislative framework. As a result, several lawsuits are being led against our
company by customers looking for their refunds. Currently, the Chargeback team is responsible for the
handling of those cases related to BR lawsuits.

When a BR lawsuit is received, the case is reviewed by the Chargeback team, and added in Fraud&CBK -
Escalations to FL queue for obtaining information in order to le an o cial reply to the lawsuit. Afterward, the
case is placed in the Refund dashboard for further actions by the Claims team. BR lawsuit-related cases will be added to the Refund dashboard with the cancellation reason "Chargeback"
by the Chargeback team and they will be labeled as "BR lawsuits". This label is for informative purposes only
and will be added automatically to the Refund dashboard and should not be used by any other department
besides the Chargeback team or for any other reason. The handling of BR lawsuits is similar to the currently existing process for standard Chargeback cases. Basically, the concept is that we claim what we can, keep the amount to us, and based on the outcome of the
lawsuit, we might later on take further actions toward customers. Almost 95 % of the cases, the BR lawsuit
case will be settled and paid out by Finance or our partners. If there ever comes a need for an exceptional
approach, the CBK team will address this matter to FL managers directly.

Chargeback
A chargeback is the name of the process when a cardholder contacts their bank to dispute a payment.

The
reason for the dispute varies and may range from the transaction being fraudulent: a promised refund
never having been received or the fact that the customer perceives the transaction amount which is higher
than the customer agreed to etc. The customer’s bank will contact ETI’s bank and depending on how compelling the dispute made by the
cardholder is, the payment may be a chargeback. Once the payment is a chargeback, our bank will have debited our bank account for the disputed amount
and the cardholder will have been reimbursed. There are two stages of the chargeback process: 
Request for information (RFI): RFI is the initial stage of the chargeback process. Chargeback (CB): A chargeback may come without the RFI stage. The most important thing to keep in mind is that once a chargeback process has started, ETI will never
refund a booking. An exception from this is if ETIs’ bank has allowed a refund to be made. The chargeback team is
responsible for retrieving the said allowance from the bank. If the bank has allowed a refund to be made
the chargeback team will state so, both in the Edvin notes and in the GDS for the relevant booking. What should Customer Care do if a customer calls?

If a customer contacts us, either by phone or mail, in regards to a refund or rebooking, and we see in the
errands that he has initiated the chargeback procedure, we inform them that we will not be able to
proceed with their request unless we receive a chargeback resolution status from the bank. This procedure is very time-consuming and may last up to 90 days after we receive a chargeback and there
is nothing we can do meanwhile to interfere or speed it up. The same process applies for all chargeback cases that have not been resolved yet, even if we come across
an errand in Edvin for a past communication (for example, the customer called for a refund and in the
meantime initiated a chargeback). We need to contact the customer again and inform them that we will not be able to process the refund
due to the chargeback made until 90 days elapse and we have the resolution status. In addition, if the
customer sends a document from the bank that the chargeback is reversed/closed, we still cannot proceed
before the 90 days elapse (because they can reopen the chargeback in that time frame). Thus, the customer will have to contact us after this period if eventually they do not receive their money
from their bank.

We will only be able to proceed if we see in Edvin that we have 'Won' the chargeback case
"Chargeback reversed", as below:
The chargeback handling can be summarized as follows:
If 90 days have passed and a Chargeback is Won, the order will have a related errand that Chargeback is
Won. If the Chargeback has been lost, the order will have a related errand "Chargeback Lost for transaction
reference : xxxx" So, if Chargeback is Lost, NO refund applies to the customer. If the customer has made a chargeback and the case is not resolved yet, we do not take any actions (ex
rebooking of any kind) or any type of refund. If the customer contacts us and the chargeback is LOST for us, the customer needs to contact directly the
bank for the refund they claimed. If the customer contacts us and the chargeback WON by us, we refund based on what we can. If we can
refund only by the rules, that's that. If we can make a full refund due to FM, we can do that. In general,
we follow our policies (any fees applied, etc). If the chargeback is won by us and the customer wants to rebook ( exible ticket included or not), if the
ticket is NOT refunded, we proceed. If the customer has purchased add-on services (for example baggage) but we were not able to add it for
some reason and the customer has led a chargeback ONLY for the second transaction corresponding to
the baggage add-on cost.

If the customer then calls for another request (for example: reissue) of the original order/transaction that
has not been disputed, you may assist the customer as per standard routines. Always make sure that the chargeback led, is only in reference to the add-on cost payment transaction. In case the chargeback is for the original order/transaction, no actions are to be taken. Proceed as per

Introduction
On the 14th of September, new legislation for the European Union is enforced on all the member countries of
the EU.
The legislation is known as Payment Services Directive 2.

What is PSD2?
PSD2 is a directive from the EU impacting mainly card transactions. It aims to make transactions within the EU
more secure as well as reduce the fraud risks involved.
One of the key aspects of PSD2 is Secure Customer Authentication (SCA). SCA asks the client to provide 2 out
of 3 identi cation methods to con rm his identity during payment via card:

Where is PSD2/SCA applicable 
The PSD2/SCA is applicable for European-issued cards used to complete the payment with a European
merchant (the merchant’s legal entity is within EU).
e.g. If a European card is used to shop from Amazon US then PSD2 is not applicable.

What does that mean for our customers? Our customers will now need to provide in most cases more than just their card number in order to complete
a purchase. For Desktop users, the customer will have to provide a one-time password which he will receive on his mobile
phone. Some banks may have ways
other than one-time passwords such as a password that customer needs to remember. For Mobile users, apart from the one–time password, there are more options instead of passwords such as a
 ngerprint or face scan. A relevant note is added on the payment page, informing the customer of the above, prior to payment:
What the customer might experience
After entering the card details and clicking on the pay/ purchase button, the customer might be redirected to
the bank’s page to provide the additional information
(password to remember or one-time password). At this point, we cannot know what the page will look like. It will di er from bank to bank, and may also ask for
di erent information. In the best-case scenario, the customer will be asked to provide the extra information required so
authentication will be applied. In the worst-case scenario, the customer will experience an error e.g. blank page, frozen screen etc. It has
